stories.title: Raj Singh gets clean chit in Shubhendu PA murder case:Police say he was picked up due to name confusion; arms supplier held
stories.summary: A man from Ballia, Raj Singh, who was arrested in the murder case of Chandranath Rath, PA to West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari, has now been given a clean chit by the CBI. The agency said he was arrested due to a confusion over his name. According to the CBI, Kolkata Police mistakenly arrested Raj Singh thinking he was the main shooter, Rajkumar Singh. Rajkumar, who is also from Ballia, was later arrested from the Chhapar toll plaza in Muzaffarnagar. The agency said Kolkata Police had first arrested two men, Vicky Maurya and Mayank Mishra, from Buxar in Bihar during the early investigation. During questioning, the name ‘Raj Singh’ came up, after which police arrested Raj from Ayodhya on May 11. UP Police had taken Raj Singh into custody and later handed him over to Bengal Police. At the time of his arrest, he was reportedly returning with family and friends after attending the wedding of an MLC in Lucknow. Soon after his arrest, several of his photos with BJP leaders went viral on social media. After his release, he has released a video. In a threatening tone, he says in the video- Jai Shri Ram. Very soon, everyone will get their answers. Please be patient. And the media... answers are coming. Wait a few days. Meanwhile, in this murder case, the CBI, with the help of UP STF, has arrested arms supplier Naveen Kumar Singh. A day before this, on Tuesday, the CBI had arrested another accused from Varanasi. The accused, Vinay Rai, is a resident of Deoria village in Ghazipur. PA Chandranath Rath was murdered on May 6, 2026. The CBI is investigating this case. The investigating agency suspects the involvement of 8 people. See 2 pictures Rajkumar Singh named Naveen during interrogation Varanasi STF Inspector Anil Kumar Singh said- Naveen Kumar Singh of Bamhanpura, Fefna police station area, Ballia, has been arrested on charges of supplying weapons to the accused in the murder of Subhendu Adhikari's PA Chandnath Rath. Naveen Kumar Singh was taken into custody by the STF from Bisunpuri intersection. During interrogation, he stated that on May 7, Gyanendra Pratap Singh alias Mannu, a resident of Sheetal Davni, came to his house. He was accompanied by the main shooters Rajkumar Singh and Golu Singh. Mannu gave him a bag and asked him to keep it at home. There were weapons in the bag. But when Rajkumar Singh was arrested, he removed the bag from the house and kept it in a warehouse. The STF recovered the bag from the warehouse. It contained one 9mm pistol, two .32 bore pistols, two .32 bore revolvers, 45 live cartridges, and nine spent casings. Suspicion of 8 people being involved in the murder According to investigative agencies, at least 8 people were involved in the conspiracy and execution of the murder. These people had conducted reconnaissance for several days before killing PA Chandranath Rath. The attackers' car had passed through Bali Toll Plaza before the murder. Here, a person in the car had paid the toll via UPI. Through the mobile number linked to this digital transaction, the police identified one accused. Then they reached the rest of the accused. Meanwhile, after initial investigation, Bengal police had suspected the involvement of contract killers in the murder of Chandranath Rath. Police had stated that Rath's murder was carried out under a plan. Professional shooters might be involved in it. Police had seized a car from the crime scene, which was used to chase Rath's Scorpio. The car's number plate turned out to be fake. The car's chassis and engine numbers were erased. Additionally, 2 bikes were involved in the attack. One of these bikes was also found near a tea shop about 4 km from the crime scene. It also had fake registration. Chandranath was with Suvendu since he was in TMC Chandranath was previously an officer in the Air Force. After taking VRS, he worked in the corporate sector for some time. After this, he entered politics. Chandranath had been working for Suvendu since he was in the Trinamool Congress. He was considered among Suvendu Adhikari's closest associates. Chandranath became part of Suvendu's official team in 2019, when Suvendu was a minister in the Mamata Banerjee government. Chandranath was responsible for Suvendu's election campaign in Bhabanipur. Bhabanipur is the same seat where Suvendu defeated Mamata Banerjee by about 15,000 votes in the assembly elections. Chandranath's mother also joined BJP with Suvendu Like Suvendu, Chandranath's family was also associated with TMC earlier. His mother, Hashi Rath, held a position in the local panchayat body in Purba Medinipur during TMC rule, but joined BJP with Suvendu Adhikari in 2020. Chandranath was calm and low-profile. He completed his studies from Rahara Ramakrishna Mission. Despite being close to Suvendu for many years, he stayed away from the limelight. Chandrakant does not have any photo with Suvendu. Understand the entire incident with a 90-minute timeline Chandranath left Kolkata around 9 AM: Chandranath was returning from Kolkata in a Scorpio to go to his rented house in Madhyamgram. The driver was driving the car. Chandranath was sitting next to him. Scorpio seen on CCTV at 10 PM: At 9:58 PM, Chandranath's Scorpio was seen passing on the road in a CCTV camera in Madhyamgram, about 20 kilometres, from Kolkata. A short while after the Scorpio passed, a car and three people on two bikes were seen following it from the area. 10:30 AM: Car blocked Scorpio's path: Near Doharia Junction in Madhyamgram, the car overtook the Scorpio and stopped in front of it. The Scorpio driver had to stop the car. Attackers on a bike started firing: Before Chandranath and his driver could understand anything, the bike-borne attackers came from the left and fired 6 to 10 rounds. Miscreants fled leaving the car: After committing the crime, the miscreants left the car there and fled on motorcycles via two different routes. Car's number plate fake: Police seized the car from the crime scene, but when the number was checked, it turned out to be fake. The car's chassis number had also been tampered with. Glock 47X pistol used in murder: The attackers had used a Glock 47X pistol. Ordinary criminals do not use such modern weapons. The way the attack happened, only a professional shooter could have carried it out.

stories.title: UP govt raises Dearness Allowance to 60%:16 lakh employees, 12 lakh pensioners to benefit from hike
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh government has increased the dearness allowance (DA) for state employees and pensioners by 2 percentage points, raising it from 58% to 60%. Around 16 lakh state employees and 12 lakh pensioners across the state will benefit from the hike. Additional Chief Secretary (Finance) Deepak Kumar said employees and pensioners would receive DA at the revised 60% rate with effect from January 1, 2026. He added that arrears for the period between January 1 and April 30 would be credited to their accounts, while the revised DA from May onwards would be paid along with June salaries and pensions. UP government increased DA twice in 2025. In the first revision in April, the DA was raised from 53% to 55%, with the revised pay made effective from 1 January 2025. In the second hike in October, the DA was further increased from 55% to 58%, with effect from 1 July 2025. How much will salaries increase? Full calculation explained Dearness Allowance (DA) is always calculated on an employee’s basic salary. Let’s understand with a simple example how much extra money this 2% hike will add to your monthly income. Assume an employee has a basic salary of ₹30,000. At 58% DA, the employee currently receives ₹17,400. With the revised 60% DA, the amount will rise to ₹18,000. This means a direct monthly increase of ₹600 in salary. Along with this, arrears for the period from January to April will also be credited together. Similarly, for senior officials with a basic salary of ₹1 lakh or more, the monthly increase in take-home pay is expected to range between ₹2,000 and ₹5,000. What is DA and why is it important? Dearness Allowance (DA) is a cost-of-living adjustment paid to government employees and pensioners. It is calculated as a percentage of the basic salary. The primary objective of DA is to protect employees’ real income against rising inflation, ensuring their salaries keep pace with increasing living costs.

stories.title: People angered by power cuts blocked Mohan-Raebareli Road:Heated argument with police; uproar at power houses all night
stories.summary: People angered by power cuts in Lucknow today, Thursday morning, blocked Mohan Road and Raebareli Road. A protest lasted for about 2 hours near Budheshwar intersection on Mohan Road. Vehicles going to the Agra Expressway were diverted from Tikunia Road. A protest lasted for about 1 hour on Raebareli Road near Utretia underpass. Protesters blocked the road using police barriers. During this, they had a heated argument with the police. Prior to this, there was chaos at various power houses throughout Wednesday night. Angry people surrounded the power houses and chanted slogans loudly. Seeing the public's anger, officers and employees of the electricity department fled from several power houses. Police arrived at the scene. Police tried to calm the people, but they remained adamant about not leaving the power houses until electricity supply was restored. It is alleged that at Faizullaganj power house, police dispersed people by brandishing sticks. Uday Raj, a contract lineman working at Faizullaganj sub-station, died due to electrocution while working on an 11,000-volt line. 3 pictures of protest on Mohan Road and Rae Bareli Road People from many colonies took to the streets In Janta Vihar, Badal Kheda and many surrounding areas, there has been a problem of power cuts for the last 3 days. Angered by this, people blocked Mohan Road near Buddheshwar intersection today morning around 8 AM. People raised slogans against the electricity department. A large number of women, youth and elderly participated in the protest. People allege that only 2 hours of electricity supply is being provided in the area out of 24 hours. Due to lack of electricity, water supply has also been completely affected. Officials are not listening to complaints People allege that complaints were made to electricity department officials many times, but the problem was not resolved. Angered by the continuous trouble, residents were forced to take to the streets and protest. Due to the protest and traffic jam on Mohan Road, long queues of vehicles formed on both sides. Pedestrians and motorists are facing great difficulties. Considering the situation, the police diverted vehicles from Tikunia Tirahe. After the police intervened, the protesters calmed down and moved off the road. Angry people blocked Rae Bareli Road Angry over continuous power cuts and faults in the PGI area, residents of Baldev Vihar, Mavaiya, and Devikheda blocked Rae Bareli Road near Utarethia underpass on Thursday morning and protested. This affected traffic for about an hour. Police, who arrived on receiving the information, had an altercation with the protesters. Later, PGI Inspector Dhirendra Singh, along with police force, persuaded the people and cleared the road. Protesters allege that power supply has been disrupted for several days in many areas connected to the Utrethia sub-station. Supply is repeatedly interrupted due to faulty transformers, burnt cables, and overloading. People warned that if the problem is not resolved, the agitation will be intensified. The electricity department has claimed to have rectified the fault. First, see 4 pictures of the commotion that happened on Wednesday midnight 400 people surrounded Utarethia Power House On Wednesday night around 11:30 PM, about 400 people surrounded the Utarethia New and Old Power Houses and protested loudly against the electricity department. People alleged that the officers and employees of the electricity department had fled from the power house. The angry people entered the power house. Upon receiving information about the commotion, the police arrived at the scene. The police tried to explain to the people, but were unsuccessful. People kept demanding restoration of electricity supply. Police chased away people at Faizullaganj Power House Power outages occurred in several areas connected to Faizullaganj Power House. Angered by this, people surrounded the power house at around 12:30 AM. They started chanting slogans, alleging power problems for 10 hours. It is alleged that upon receiving information, the police reached the spot. The police reportedly used batons to disperse the people from the power house. ABC cable burnt in Nadarganj The power supply to the area was disrupted due to the burning of the ABC cable in front of Sarojini Nagar Block Nadarganj Power House. Consumers are highly agitated due to hours of power cuts. People allege that despite overload and dilapidated infrastructure, the department does not make timely improvements, for which the public is suffering. Angry people also created a ruckus at Telibagh Power House due due to lack of electricity. The enraged people came out onto the streets. Problem in Gomti Nagar Extension for 3 days The incident of cables burning continuously for 3 days has come to light at the power house located in Gomti Nagar Extension Sector 5. This is disrupting the electricity supply to people's homes. When the power went out in the area late Wednesday night, people reached the power house and protested vehemently. Meanwhile, after the police arrived and calmed them down, people quieted down after a long time. People have accused electricity department officials of negligence. People argued with JE The power supply to many areas connected to the BBAU power house also went out on Wednesday night. Angered people reached the power house around 12 midnight. People created a ruckus. There was a heated argument between the people and the JE present at the power house. People said that the supply to all areas connected to the power house should be restored, otherwise the supply should be completely stopped. Contract worker dies while repairing line Contractual lineman Uday Raj, working at Faizullaganj sub-station, died on Wednesday night after being electrocuted while working on an 11,000-volt line. According to fellow employee Pankaj Parmar, Uday Raj had gone to repair a transformer near Neelkanth Temple. While climbing the high-tension line, he received a severe electric shock, causing him to fall from the pole. In serious condition, he was immediately taken to KGMU Trauma Center, where doctors declared him dead during treatment. Following the incident, there is widespread grief among electricity employees. stories.title: ‘Sell cows on Go-LX, not to butchers’:Shankaracharya says, 'We will buy protect cows'
stories.summary: Swami Avimukteshwaranand on Thursday announced the launch of a new platform named “Go-LX”, aimed at preventing cows from being sold for slaughter. Comparing the initiative to OLX, the Shankaracharya said the website would allow cattle breeders and traders to advertise cows for sale, while cow protectors and devotees could purchase them for care and protection. Releasing a video message, he said the platform was created at the request of Hindus and would work to ensure that cows do not end up in slaughterhouses under any circumstances. “If any Hindu wants to sell their cow, sell it to me. We are ready to buy. We will not let cows be slaughtered,” he said, adding that the initiative seeks to counter claims that Hindu cattle breeders would face economic hardship if Muslims stopped consuming beef. The Shankaracharya said no “true Hindu” would knowingly sell a cow for slaughter and welcomed members of the Muslim community who support a ban on cow slaughter. According to him, several Muslims have stated that consuming beef is not an obligatory religious practice in Islam. He said ending cow slaughter and beef consumption would strengthen social harmony and mutual goodwill. Calling cow protection a symbol of Indian culture, compassion and eternal values, he added that several Hindu organisations and cow devotees across the country have extended support to the campaign.

stories.title: 5 Bullets fired at history-sheeter in Prayagraj:Police probe points to old dispute over setting up shop at Sangam
stories.summary: A history-sheeter was shot dead in Prayagraj early on Thursday morning. The incident took place in the Mutthiganj area at around 5 AM. According to police, the accused called 35-year-old Saksham Panda out of his house and shot him five times from close range. Local residents tried to catch the attacker, but he managed to escape. After getting information, Saksham’s family rushed him to the hospital, where doctors declared him dead. Police later arrested the accused, identified as Bhole Punjabi, from his house. During questioning, he told police that Saksham had allegedly set fire to his worship stall in the Sangam area on Wednesday. An argument had taken place between the two over the issue. Police said Bhole called Saksham for a discussion on Thursday morning, but during the conversation, another argument broke out, after which he opened fire on him. See pictures related to the incident- The history-sheeter used to perform rituals and prayers at the ghats Saksham Panda was a resident of Malviya Nagar, under the Mutthiganj police station area. He used to perform rituals and prayers at the ghats. Saksham's mother said that on Wednesday night, her son had dinner with the family and then went to sleep. On Thursday morning, someone called, and he left the house. A short while later, it was learned that her son had been murdered. When we reached the spot, he was lying on the ground, covered in blood. Accused attacked a history-sheeter 3 months ago The family members allege that Saksham Panda was fired upon in Malviya Nagar locality on March 12. Saksham and his friend Ravi Panda were injured in this attack. A case was registered against several people, including Vimal Panda and Bhole Punjabi, in the matter. The police had arrested Bhole Punjabi and sent him to jail, while they were searching for Vimal Panda. One month later, on April 12, Bhole Punjabi came out of jail on bail.

stories.title: 400-metre-long queue for OPD registration at KGMU:Heatstroke patients increasing rapidly; severe heat leaves people distressed
stories.summary: The intense heat in Lucknow is increasing the problems of patients in both private and government hospitals. From getting OPD slips made to admitting serious patients, people are facing long delays and heavy crowds. Hospital administrations claim that arrangements are under control, but patients and their attendants continue to struggle. Long queues can be seen at almost every major hospital in the city. Cases of heatstroke, dehydration and other heat-related illnesses are rising rapidly. More than 100 such patients are reaching major government hospitals every day, including KGMU, Lohia Institute, Civil Hospital, Lokbandhu, Balrampur, Dufferin and Ram Sagar Mishra Hospital. At KGMU, a nearly 400-metre-long queue for patient registration was seen from the morning itself, showing the growing pressure on the health system due to the heatwave. See 2 pictures Diarrhea increasing in children In government hospitals, children from newborns to 14 years of age are falling prey to diarrhea, dehydration, and fever. In the pediatric OPDs of many hospitals, 20% more children are arriving compared to normal days. Doctors say that about 50% of the children coming to the OPD are complaining of dehydration, vomiting, diarrhea, abdominal pain, and fever. The number of sick children has also increased in the emergency. Many children have to be admitted and treated. Most children in hospital pediatric wards are suffering from vomiting, diarrhoea, and fever. Abdominal problems increasing due to infection Dr. Rajesh Srivastava, a specialist at Civil Hospital, said - The risk of infection has increased due to rising temperatures. Bacterial infections are increasing stomach-related problems. About 100 children are arriving daily at the hospital's OPD, of whom more than half are suffering from diarrhoea and dehydration. He said that if children have vomiting, diarrhoea, and fever, give medicine only on the doctor's advice and do not give antibiotics on your own. How many patients are coming? Long queues extending to the main road at KGMU Long queues of patients are visible outside the CMS office in the New OPD complex. These include the elderly, women, small children, and patients suffering from serious illnesses. Amidst the scorching sun and humidity, people are forced to wait for hours for their turn, but adequate arrangements to provide them relief are not visible. Patients and their relatives say that OPD registration counters open at 8 AM, but people arrive much earlier, hoping to get an early turn. Many people come to the hospital premises at night itself to secure a place further ahead in the morning queue. Due to the heat, elderly patients and children are facing the most difficulty. Many patients standing in the queue are experiencing problems like dizziness, weakness, and dehydration. Despite this, there are neither adequate arrangements nor any provision for cold drinking water visible on the premises. Increasing number of heatstroke patients Dr. Rajiv Dixit, Director of Rajnarayan Lokbandhu Combined Hospital, stated that the number of heatstroke patients in hospitals is increasing. Separate wards have been created for them. Additionally, arrangements for ice packs have also been made. Claims failed, online system collapsed Many patients reported that despite the facility of online registration, patients and their attendants are unable to avail its benefits due to technical difficulties. Consequently, a large number of patients queue up directly to get their slips made. Among them, people coming from far-flung districts start their journey at night itself to get treatment early in the morning. Health experts say that standing in the open for a long time in the scorching heat increases the risk of heatstroke and dehydration. 10-bed ward is reserved in the civil hospital Heatstroke fatal for heart, kidney, and liver patients

stories.title: Jamrani Dam canals to be made wildlife-friendly:Stairs for elephants and tunnels for snakes to be made; lakhs in Uttarakhand and UP to get water
stories.summary: The long-pending Jamrani Dam Project, which remained stalled for nearly 50 years, is now being developed not only as an irrigation and drinking water project but also as a model for wildlife conservation. Special elephant corridors, wide stairways and underground passages for reptiles, including snakes, are being constructed along the Haripura Canal passing through the Tanda forest to ensure that natural wildlife routes remain undisturbed. The project, estimated to cost around ₹3,808 crore, is expected to address drinking water needs in Haldwani and Kathgodam while also supplying irrigation water to thousands of farmers in Uttar Pradesh. The scheme, whose foundation stone was laid in 1976 but remained stuck in files for decades, is now progressing rapidly on the ground. Authorities aim to complete construction by July 2029. Officials said the objective is not just to deliver water infrastructure but also to maintain a balance between development and environmental conservation. 15-km Haripura Canal under construction Under the Jamrani Dam project, a 15-kilometre-long Haripura Canal is being constructed to supply water to the Haripura reservoir. Project officials said around 7km of the canal has already been completed, while the remaining 8km stretch passes through forest land. This section is considered the most technically and environmentally challenging part of the project. A proposal seeking permission to cut around 1,000 trees in the forest area is currently pending with the government. Meanwhile, the Forest Department is preparing a Wildlife Conservation Plan for the area. Officials said the remaining canal construction is expected to be completed within one year after approvals are granted. Elephant corridors being developed in forest stretch The Tanda forest is regarded as a natural habitat for elephants, tigers, deer and several other wildlife species. Project authorities said one of the biggest challenges was ensuring that the traditional movement routes of elephants were not blocked after the canal’s construction. To address this, special elephant corridors are being created at four locations along the 8km forest stretch. At these points, the canal will be covered and pathways built above it to allow wildlife to cross safely. In addition, wide and reinforced stairways are being constructed along the canal banks for elephants. According to AK Khare, the design has been prepared specifically to ensure safe wildlife movement, while the Forest Department will independently undertake additional conservation work using project funds. Underground passages for snakes and reptiles Officials said the project also focuses on protecting smaller wildlife species. Special underground “reptile passes” are being built beneath the canal for snakes and other crawling animals. Large hume pipes are being laid underground to connect both sides of the canal, allowing reptiles to safely move across the forest without entering the water channel. Forest officials believe blocking natural animal routes could increase human-wildlife conflict in nearby areas. The reptile-pass model has therefore been adopted to minimise such risks. Irrigation water to reach 684 villages The project’s benefits will extend beyond Uttarakhand into neighbouring Uttar Pradesh. After completion, irrigation water is expected to reach more than 1.15 lakh hectares of farmland across 684 villages in Bareilly and Rampur districts. Agricultural areas in Uttarakhand’s Terai and Bhabar regions are also expected to benefit significantly. For farmers long dependent on rainfall, officials say the project could provide a permanent irrigation solution. Authorities claim it will increase agricultural production and improve farmers’ incomes. Major relief expected for Haldwani and Kathgodam With rapid population growth, drinking water shortages in Haldwani and Kathgodam have intensified over the years. Water scarcity during summer has become a recurring problem in several areas. Officials consider the Jamrani Dam one of the most important drinking water projects for the Kumaon region. After completion, the project aims to supply 117 MLD (million litres per day) of drinking water to nearly 10.5 lakh people. For this purpose, uninterrupted water supply will be ensured up to the Haripura reservoir. Experts believe the project will play a major role in addressing Haldwani’s long-term water crisis. Project remained stalled for five decades The foundation stone for the Jamrani Dam Project was laid on February 26, 1976. However, due to environmental clearances, technical complications and funding-related hurdles, the project remained delayed for decades. Initially estimated at around ₹61 crore, the project cost has now increased to nearly ₹3,808 crore. Construction work is currently underway at full pace. Officials said the dam height has been fixed at 150.6 metres, while the project will create a lake stretching nearly 10 kilometres. Construction of new canals and renovation of old canal systems are also underway. The project is being implemented under the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchai Yojana (PMKSY). The Central Government is bearing 90 per cent of the project cost, while the remaining expenditure will be shared by the Uttarakhand and Uttar Pradesh governments. Tourism and employment opportunities expected Local residents believe the 10-kilometre-long lake likely to form after the dam’s completion could emerge as a major tourist attraction. People expect tourism-related activities such as boating, hotels and local businesses to receive a boost in surrounding areas. The project has already generated employment opportunities during the construction phase. Locals also expect future tourism growth to create additional jobs for young people in the region.

stories.title: OBC panel formed ahead of UP panchayat polls:Retired judge Ram Avtar Singh gets charge to frame reservation report
stories.summary: The UP government has constituted the State Local Rural Body Dedicated Backwards Classes Commission (OBC Commission) for the Panchayat elections. The commission's tenure will be 6 months. Retired Justice Ram Autar Singh of the Allahabad High Court has been made the chairman of the commission. Additionally, 2 retired Additional District Judges (Brijesh Kumar, Santosh Vishwakarma) and 2 retired IAS officers (Dr. Arvind Chaurasia and SP Singh) have been included in the commission. The commission's report may come by November 2026. After this, the reservation will be decided. It has become clear that Panchayat elections will only be possible after the Assembly elections of 2027. On February 4, 2025, the High Court had ordered the government to constitute the commission. The chairman of the commission and both retired Additional District Judges have previously served as chairmen of the OBC Commission constituted in 2022 for determining reservation for backward classes in urban local body elections. The commission led by Singh had submitted its report within three months. The Supreme Court also agreed with this report and gave the green light for conducting the local body elections. Retired IAS Dr. Arvind Chaurasia and SP Singh have been included as new members. All members in the commission, except SP Singh, are from backward classes. Chairman Ram Autar Singh comes from the Jat community. Meanwhile, Santosh Kumar Vishwakarma is from the Lohar community, Brijesh Kumar Swarnkar, and Dr. Arvind Chaurasia are from their respective communities. Chairman Ram Autar Singh told Dainik Bhaskar: The commission's office will be established soon. After that, I will take charge of my duties. The commission will talk to all sections of society and visit districts. After this, a report will be prepared. The commission will strive to present the report before the stipulated deadline. Commission Chairman, a resident of Bijnor, served as High Court Judge for 3 years Commission Chairman Ram Autar Singh was born on January 15, 1949, in Bijnor. He started his career in PCS (Judicial Service) in 1976. In 1991, he was promoted to Higher Judicial Service. In 2005, he became a District Judge. Thereafter, he served as a Judge in the Allahabad High Court from 2008 to 2011. Meanwhile, retired IAS Dr. Arvind Kumar Chaurasia was promoted from PCS to IAS in 2012. He has also served as the District Magistrate of Lakhimpur. Additionally, he has worked as Special Secretary in the Irrigation Department. Why was the Backward Class Commission formed? Based on the report and survey of the Backward Class Commission, it will be decided which Panchayat seat in your area will be reserved for OBC (female or male) and which will remain general. In fact, the Supreme Court had stated that before providing OBC reservation in local bodies (such as Gram Panchayat, Zila Panchayat), states must complete the process after a 'Triple Test', i.e., a three-tier investigation. This commission has been formed to complete this triple test. The commission will collect data on the OBC community. If the government had directly implemented the reservation without the commission's report, the matter could have been stuck in court and the panchayat elections could have been halted. With the formation of the commission, elections can now be conducted in a legally secure manner. The commission will have 3 main tasks- Collecting data- The commission will investigate the population of backward classes in local bodies (at block and panchayat levels) and their need for political representation. A report will be prepared on this basis. Adhering to the 50% limit- The commission will ensure that the total reservation for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and Other Backward Classes combined does not exceed 50%. Determining the reservation ratio- Based on the commission's recommendations, the number of reserved seats in each local body will be determined according to the proportion of the OBC population. Term of Panchayat members completing this month The last Panchayat elections in UP were held in 2021. The 5-year term of the Panchayats is completing by May 25-26, 2026. According to constitutional rules, new elections should have been completed before the expiry of the current term. This means Panchayat elections in UP were scheduled to be held before May 2026 or in the month of May itself. However, before the announcement of elections in UP, the matter reached the High Court. The High Court ordered fresh reservation by forming an OBC commission. This is why elections will be held a year late this time. In such a situation, the Panchayati Raj Department has sent a proposal to the Cabinet for the appointment of an administrator or the formation of an administrative committee to manage affairs after the term of the village heads (Gram Pradhans) ends. The proposal may get approval in a few days. However, about two months ago, in an interview given to Bhaskar, Panchayati Raj Minister Om Prakash Rajbhar had said that the Panchayat elections would be held by July 12.

Mayawati refuses to meet Congress delegation:Leaders reached without prior notice; discussion starts again on BSP-Congress tie-up in UP
stories.summary: Congress's attempt to form an alliance behind the scenes with BSP chief Mayawati backfired. On May 19 (Tuesday), the Congress Scheduled Caste (SC) department national president Rajendra Pal Gautam, MP Tanuj Punia, and other leaders suddenly arrived to meet Mayawati. However, Mayawati did not meet them. She sent them back from the gate. Returning empty-handed from the BSP chief's residence created a storm in UP politics. Congress MP Imran Masood himself reprimanded his leaders. He said, I am in favor of meetings and interactions in politics, but arriving to meet without an appointment like this was wrong. Is Congress exploring the possibility of an alliance with BSP in UP, leaving SP? Why did Imran Masood give the example of Bengal on SP chief Akhilesh Yadav's formula of offering 'guaranteed winning seats'? Congress leaders wrote down their mobile numbers and returned A meeting of the Congress Scheduled Caste Department was held at the Congress headquarters in Lucknow on May 19. After this, the national president of the department, Rajendra Pal Gautam, Congress MP from Barabanki, Tanuj Punia, and other leaders suddenly reached Mayawati's house. They asked the security guard at the gate to call Mayawati's private secretary, Mewalal Gautam. They requested an appointment to meet Mayawati. According to sources, Congress leaders waited at the gate for about 10 minutes. Then a message came from inside that Behan ji (Mayawati) was busy and the meeting would not be possible now. After this, the Congress leaders wrote their names and mobile numbers at the gate and left. However, pictures of this attempted meeting by Congress leaders went viral. After this, there was a stir in politics. Political meanings began to be drawn from this meeting. News spread that Congress was exploring possibilities of an alliance with BSP, leaving SP, in the UP assembly elections. Rahul Gandhi was also in Raebareli on May 19. In such a situation, it was directly claimed that these leaders wanted to meet Mayawati with a message from him. Both leaders also have a background linked to BSP Among the Congress leaders who arrived to meet Mayawati, Rajendra Prasad Gautam has been an old BSP member. After leaving BSP, he joined the Aam Aadmi Party and then Congress. Barabanki MP Tanuj Punia is the son of senior Congress leader and former MP PL Punia. When Mayawati was Chief Minister, PL Punia was her principal secretary. At that time, he held significant influence among UP bureaucrats. This is why political analysts are not considering it a normal meeting. They are considering it part of the secret diplomacy of the alliance. Mayawati's denial certainly put a question mark on Congress's strategy. There is a discussion in political circles that the BSP chief will not agree to an alliance through any leader below the level of Rahul Gandhi or Priyanka Gandhi. The sudden, uninvited attempt by Congress leaders to meet her probably did not please Mayawati. Why is Congress exploring possibilities of an alliance with BSP in UP? Senior journalist Syed Qasim says - Congress feels that it will not get the desired seats in an alliance with SP. SP chief Akhilesh Yadav himself had given a statement regarding the 2027 assembly elections at an event on May 19. He had said that he would give seats to alliance partners based on the Lok Sabha election formula. In this, the formula would be a guarantee of victory, not just a seat. While Congress wants to strengthen itself in UP. Congress wants 125 assembly seats, with at least one seat in every district. SP wants to contest around 350 seats itself in UP. It feels that if it contests fewer seats, it will be difficult to defeat BJP. SP also cites examples of Bihar, Tamil Nadu, West Bengal, and Assam. Imran Masood recalled Bengal results On May 20, Congress MP Imran Masood from Saharanpur reacted to Akhilesh's statement. He said, "I would say, no seat, no victory. When there are no seats, where will the victory come from? Everyone should think about this. Especially, such people should learn a lesson from the Bengal results." If it had been fought strategically in Bengal, the India alliance would have won the election. What the Election Commission did is a different matter. This kind of mistake must be avoided in UP. However, he did not name the SP during this time. Congress had to do damage control after BSP's stance After returning empty-handed from Mayawati's house, Congress went into damage control mode. UP Congress President Ajay Rai clarified on May 20, saying, "This was a personal program of those leaders. No official order was given by the party." Ajay Rai's statement further increased the confusion. On one hand, Congress wants an alliance with BSP, on the other hand, the party is trying to back down by calling it 'personal'. Rajendra Pal Gautam himself said that Mayawati is the former Chief Minister of the Dalit community. That's why he went to meet her to inquire about her well-being. Tanuj Punia also called it a "general visit". He said that Behan Ji is a senior leader of our community. She is 70 years old. We went to inquire about her health. SP chief alerted after Tamil Nadu incident SP is on alert after the Tamil Nadu incident. Akhilesh also does not agree with the way Congress broke its 22-year-old alliance and immediately joined TVK after the results. Now, as Congress leaders tried to meet Mayawati, he must have become even more cautious. SP chief Akhilesh Yadav made a measured post on X on May 20. He also reminded Congress of its weak organization in UP. He conveyed the message that Congress benefited from SP's strong organization in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, which is why it was able to win 6 seats.

stories.title: 9 UP leaders in BJP national executive race:Harish Dwivedi gains ground after Assam success strategy; Kataria seen as key Gurjar face
stories.summary: Major changes are likely in the national organisation of the Bharatiya Janata Party. Preparations are underway for the announcement of the new national team under party president Nitin Naveen, who took charge on January 20, 2026. The new team is being closely watched in political circles. Party sources say young leaders may get more importance this time to ensure better coordination between the president and office bearers. Sources also said the BJP is preparing its team while keeping the 2027 Assembly elections in mind. Leaders from different caste groups in Uttar Pradesh may be included to maintain social balance. One Brahmin, one Thakur, one Vaishya and 2-3 leaders from backward classes are likely to get a place in the new team. Know about the changes in the national team Currently, many big names from UP are included in BJP's national team, in which there are indications of major changes this time- These 9 big contenders from UP for the 'Naveen' team Strength: He is very close to PM Modi, Amit Shah, BL Santosh, and Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath in the central leadership. He played a crucial role as in-charge in forming the BJP government in Assam and Tripura. Strength: He was the strategist behind the one-sided victory in the Assam elections and is close to Amit Shah. Recently, he was also a strong contender for the post of UP State President. Strength: Extremely trusted by the top leaders of the organization and the Sangh (RSS) (BL Santosh, Arun Kumar). Currently working as a bridge between the government, the Sangh, and the organization. Strength: A big 'Gurjar' face of the BJP. To thwart SP's attempts to infiltrate the Gurjar vote bank, he may get an important position in the national team. Strength: Gupta, who started his journey as an ordinary worker, is an expert in election management. He is a prominent leader of the Vaishya community. Recently, he was also in the running for state president and cabinet expansion. Strength: He has been continuously active in the organisation since 2010. He has long experience in implementing programs at the grassroots level and in election management. Good hold in the Sangh. Strength: Close to former Governor Kalraj Mishra and trusted by Home Minister Amit Shah. Long experience in the media in charge and as a spokesperson. Strength: Comes from the Bhumihar community. In charge of PM Modi's parliamentary constituency, Varanasi. Has successfully completed many major campaigns. Strength: A prominent Brahmin face from Western UP. He has been the former National Media in charge. Currently, he is handling the responsibility as the In-charge of Himachal Pradesh. Significance of being included in BJP's National Executive - UP organisation will also change. Pankaj Chaudhary's list is ready Along with the national team, the announcement of UP's new state executive may also happen soon. Pankaj Chaudhary, who became the state president on December 14, 2025, has gone to Delhi with his new list. Along with the state executive, several regional presidents will be replaced after reviewing their performance. Amidst discussions of sending stalwarts like Santosh Singh, Vijay Bahadur Pathak, Amarpal Maurya, and Kanta Kardam to the central organisation, new and diligent workers will be given a place in the state organisation.

stories.title: Ballia salary scam exposes fake appointments:Peons worked as Shiksha Mitras too, crores paid despite recruitment ban
stories.summary: Rameshwar Singh is a peon at Ramkaran Inter College in Bhimpura town, Ballia. His appointment was on July 1, 2005. Surprisingly, Rameshwar has also been deployed as a Shikshamitra (para-teacher) in the town's Composite School since August 23, 2015. He is drawing a salary and honorarium for both positions. Similarly, his real nephew, Shivamangal Singh, is also a peon in the same college. Additionally, he is a Shikshamitra in a government school in the town. Shivamangal's wife, Vibha Singh, is also a peon in the same college. In Ballia, 179 such fraudulent appointments were made, and 45 crore rupees in salary and arrears were paid. In Azamgarh, Jaunpur, Mau, and Agra too, 194 fake peons, clerks, and teachers are looting the government treasury by securing jobs with forged documents. Despite the Education Director's ban, crores of rupees in salaries are being paid. Nephew is older than his real uncle The details of Shivamangal Singh, who is drawing a peon's salary and Shikshamitra's honorarium in Bhimpura, and his real uncle Rameshwar Singh are available on the Manav Sampada portal. It is known that Rameshwar became a Shikshamitra from the 'Ex-Serviceman' quota. This means he has also served in the army. DIOS who filed the FIR are themselves breaking the rules The story begins in 2018. Ramesh Singh, who served as District Inspector of Schools (DIOS) in Ballia between 2018 and 2022, made appointments to 179 posts of peons, clerks, and teachers in secondary schools and Sanskrit secondary schools. Many sons and relatives of influential people were among them. Assistant teachers were also recruited in non-aided Sanskrit secondary schools by showing attachments. Then, salaries were also released from the treasury. On July 5, 2024, when Devendra Kumar Gupta became DIOS, he stopped the salaries of these 179 fraudulently appointed individuals in July itself. Additionally, on September 9, he informed the then Additional Chief Secretary (ACS) by writing a letter. He had written - Ramesh Singh has made permanent appointments by showing backdates, despite the outsourcing rules applicable to the recruitment of peons. Devendra Gupta filed an FIR at Ballia Kotwali in February 2025, regarding the disappearance of files related to 179 fake appointments. Former DIOS Ramesh Singh, his assistant Sanjay Kumar Kunwar, Senior Assistant Ajay Singh, Urdu translator Muhammad Mainuddin, and Head Clerk Shivanand Tiwari were named as accused in the case. Following this, all 179 people went to court regarding the withholding of their salaries. The High Court ordered an investigation into the matter and payment on January 8, 2026. Taking advantage of this, the current DIOS Devendra Kumar Gupta paid salaries and arrears amounting to Rs 45 crore to all 179 people by March 2026. High Court ordered an investigation by forming a committee 27 petitions related to this matter reached the High Court. On January 8, 2026, the High Court also ordered the formation of a committee to investigate the 179 fake appointments. It had said - there is a dispute over the appointments and salaries are being paid from the government treasury. In such a situation, it becomes important that an investigation be conducted by forming a committee. The order also stated that any salary being issued would be investigated. If irregularities are found, the payment will be recovered. The order included the Director of Secondary Education, the Financial Controller, and the District School Inspectors of Ballia, Agra, Azamgarh, and Mau in the committee. The High Court had stated that the committee would issue notices to all management committees and principals of inter colleges, demanding documents related to appointments. A period of 3 weeks was given for this. Colleges had to submit the documents within 2 weeks of receiving the notice. There was also an order to seek the help of the Inspector General (IG) of CBCID if needed during the investigation of the documents. The committee had to prepare its report 4 weeks after receiving the documents. Based on this, the Directorate of Education had to decide whether the appointment of 179 employees was valid or invalid. On the order of the High Court, the Director of Secondary Education formed a Special Investigation Team (SIT) on February 4, 2026. On February 5, documents related to 179 appointments and a report were requested from Ballia DIOS Devendra Gupta. Which has not been sent by Ballia DIOS till date. Due to this, the investigation could not be completed. No trace of the SIT investigation formed in 2025 either Before this, on January 20, 2025, Special Secretary Yogesh Kumar had formed a two-member SIT to investigate fake appointments made in non-governmental aided secondary and Sanskrit schools in Ballia, Agra, Azamgarh and Jaunpur. It included Director General of School Education Kanchan Verma and CBCID IG M. Rajesh Kumar. Additionally, the Additional Chief Secretary (Secondary Education) was instructed to provide the documents of all individuals with fake appointments to the SIT. The education mafia of Ballia filed a writ petition in the Lucknow bench of the High Court to stop this SIT investigation. Then, Special Secretary Yogesh Kumar stated in an affidavit submitted to the court that the SIT investigation was very close to completion. On this, the court ordered the SIT investigation to continue and to investigate all four districts, including Ballia. However, even after more than a year has passed since then, there is no trace of the SIT's investigation report. ACS stopped payment, DIOS released ₹45 crore Then Additional Director of Education Surendra Kumar Tiwari had stopped the salary payment of 179 fraudulently appointed personnel in Ballia on February 13, 2026. Despite this, DIOS Devendra Gupta released ₹45 crore as salaries for all 179 employees in March. In response, it was stated that the salary was paid on the basis of a contempt notice issued by the High Court. Whereas, the court should have been informed of the entire matter in the contempt petition, which was not done. Despite DM's recommendation, Devendra is posted in Ballia Ballia District Magistrate Mangala Prasad Singh had written a letter to the government regarding salary payments etc. on behalf of DIOS Devendra Gupta. In this, considering Devendra Gupta's retirement on May 31, he had recommended attaching him to the directorate. Despite this, Devendra remains stationed in Ballia. It is alleged that before retirement, he is making arrear payments to 179 employees by taking a 25% commission. Several audio clips of this are also viral. In this matter, Congress MLA Virendra Chaudhary from Pharenda, Maharajganj district, complained to CM Yogi Adityanath on April 6, 2026. Jobs were also distributed to close relatives of influential people for 179 posts

stories.title: UP heatwave worsens as 23 districts on red alert:Banda hits highest 48°C again amid severe hot winds
stories.summary: UP has been in the grip of a heatwave for a week. Banda remained the hottest city in the country for the fourth consecutive day, where the maximum temperature was recorded at 48 degrees Celsius. On Wednesday, the temperature in Prayagraj was 46.4 °C, in Jhansi 45.9 °C, in Agra 45.3 °C, in Bulandshahr 45 °C, and in Kanpur 44.6 °C. On Thursday, most cities in UP are experiencing strong sunshine since morning. People are suffering from the heat. Today, there is a heatwave alert in 59 districts of the state. Among these, 23 districts have a red alert for heatwave. This means that conditions could become severe due to hot winds here. The effect of the heat is also visible on animals. In Etawah Safari, ACs have been installed in some lion enclosures, and coolers in others. In Noida, a monkey was seen swimming in a swimming pool. In Lucknow Zoo, water is being used to cool down the animals. The Meteorological Department says that dry and hot winds coming from Balochistan in Pakistan and the Thar Desert are directly reaching the plains of North India. Because of this, heat like the last week of May or June is being felt already. Lucknow's meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh said- There is a possibility of severe heatwave across the state for the next one week. Nights will also be warm in Western UP. In the coming days, a rise of 2 to 3 degrees in temperature can be observed. Only leave home in the afternoon if there is a very important task. Around 11 proposals are expected to be approved in the meeting, including two key ones. The first is the formation of an OBC Commission for conducting three-tier panchayat elections. The Lucknow bench of the Allahabad High Court had directed the formation of this commission. Panchayat elections in the state will be held only after the commission submits its report. The second major proposal is related to students studying veterinary science. Their internship stipend is proposed to be increased from ₹4,000 per month to ₹12,000 per month. Around 2,000 to 2,500 students take admission every year in BVSc AH (Bachelor of Veterinary Science) courses in state colleges. Including all batches, more than 10,000 veterinary students are currently studying in Uttar Pradesh. This will be the first Cabinet meeting after the expansion of the government. However, two newly appointed cabinet ministers Bhupendra Chaudhary and Manoj Pandey have not yet been allotted departments. Chief Secretary S.P. Goyal issued the meeting agenda on Sunday evening. stories.title: Kanpur man who murdered twin daughters attempts suicide in jail:Slits throat with sharpened steel plate; claims he was not provided depression treatment
stories.summary: The accused in the Kanpur twin daughters murder case, Shashiranjan Mishra, attempted suicide inside jail on Sunday by slitting his throat. Fellow inmates saw him writhing in pain and informed the jail administration. He was immediately admitted to Ursala Hospital for treatment. According to doctors, Shashiranjan is out of danger, but he has been referred to Halat Hospital for better treatment. Meanwhile, the jail administration has also started investigating the entire incident. Made it sharp by rubbing on the ground under the pretext of cleaning the plate Shashiranjan Mishra, a medicine trader living in Trimurti Apartment behind Mickey House in Kanpur’s Kidwai Nagar area, had allegedly slit the throats of his 11-year-old twin daughters on the night of April 19. After the murders, he could not gather the courage to die by suicide himself and instead informed police and surrendered. Since then, the accused had been lodged in Kanpur jail. On Sunday afternoon, Shashiranjan allegedly tried to slit his throat using a steel plate. However, inmates present there noticed him and overpowered him. Following the information, jail authorities admitted him to Ursala Hospital. At the hospital, Shashiranjan claimed that he did not know what exactly had happened to him. He said he was suffering from depression and was not receiving treatment inside jail, due to which the incident occurred. After primary treatment, he was referred to Halat Hospital for advanced care. Doctors said his condition was out of danger after examination. The jail superintendent said that Shashiranjan had been under depression ever since killing his daughters. He had allegedly been sharpening his steel plate every day by rubbing it on the ground under the pretext of cleaning it. After sharpening it over several days, he allegedly went into the jail bathroom on Sunday and attempted suicide by slitting his throat. Other inmates heard his screams and rushed there, after which the matter came to light. He was then admitted to Ursala Hospital for treatment, where doctors declared him out of danger. Killed daughters being fed up with harassment Shashiranjan alleged that two residents of his society, Joginder Singh and BD Dixit, used to harass him. He claimed Joginder Singh had grabbed Rs 12 lakh and BD Dixit Rs 5 lakh from him. According to him, the money was taken in the name of selling a flat, but neither was the flat handed over nor was the money returned. He alleged that he wanted to vacate the flat, but was not being allowed to do so. He further claimed that the two men used to abuse him and his daughters and had made his life miserable. He said he was a depression patient and suffered from severe depressive episodes, but his treatment was not continuing inside jail. He claimed that Sunday’s incident also occurred during a depressive episode. He said he did not realise what was happening and felt as if voices were coming from his head. “I felt surrounded by many people and could hear loud noises. I am in depression,” he reportedly said.

stories.title: UP to recruit 20,000 teachers, instructors:Women staff to get 6-month maternity leave, says CM Yogi
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Sunday handed over cheques of revised honorarium to 24,717 instructors at Lok Bhavan. The state government has increased their honorarium from Rs 9,000 to Rs 17,000 with effect from April 1, 2026. During the programme, CM Yogi also announced the recruitment of 20,000 new teachers and instructors. He said a demand has already been sent for the recruitment of 10,000 new teachers, while new instructors will also be appointed in upper primary schools. The Chief Minister said that although a foundation is not visible, its strength is extremely important. He added that basic teachers, Shiksha Mitras and part-time instructors form the foundation of the education department, and therefore their honorarium should be respectable. A total of 41,307 instructors were recruited in 2011-12 and deployed in 13,769 middle schools to teach children. At that time, they were receiving Rs 7,000 per month. At present, there are 24,296 instructors working in the state. The government had increased the honorarium of instructors by Rs 2,000 in 2022, and has now raised it from Rs 9,000 to Rs 17,000. The government has also extended cashless health insurance coverage of up to Rs 5 lakh to instructors. Women instructors will additionally receive six months of maternity leave. School dropout rate reduced from 18% to 3% CM Yogi said that earlier the dropout rate in Uttar Pradesh schools was around 17-18%, meaning 17 to 18 out of every 100 children used to leave studies midway. He said the state has now succeeded in reducing it to nearly 3%. He added that the number of children enrolling in schools is continuously increasing and recruitment of basic teachers and instructors will also continue. He said the basic education system earlier suffered from disorder, but has now undergone transformation. Every child has talent, needs right direction not scolding The Chief Minister said every child has hidden potential and children should be guided properly instead of being beaten or humiliated. He said students should be encouraged towards cleanliness, discipline and good values. He added that if children help in maintaining cleanliness in schools, they should be rewarded instead of punished. CM Yogi also said that making such videos and circulating them on social media is not appropriate. Children should be nurtured into confident, strong and positive individuals, he added. Appeal to walk with PM Modi amid global crisis Yogi Adityanath said the Iran-US tensions are affecting the entire world and inflation has reached extreme levels even in resource-rich countries like the United States. He said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, India took timely and important decisions. The Chief Minister appealed to people to stand with PM Modi keeping national interest in mind during the period of global challenges. Instructors' honorarium was doubled in 2017, not implemented The honorarium of instructors was increased from around Rs 9,000 to Rs 17,000 in 2017, but the decision was not implemented after the change in government. Instructors later filed a petition in the Lucknow bench of the High Court. Former Justice Rajesh Singh Chauhan of the Lucknow High Court’s single bench had ordered payment of Rs 17,000 honorarium along with 9% interest to instructors. The state government challenged the order through an appeal. The High Court’s double bench directed payment of Rs 17,000 honorarium for only one year, after which the matter reached the Supreme Court. On February 5, the Supreme Court dismissed the Uttar Pradesh government’s appeal against increasing the honorarium of instructors. The apex court also ordered that instructors’ jobs should not be terminated. The Supreme Court’s double bench clearly stated that instructors would continue in service even after the contractual term ends. It observed that since they had been working continuously for 10 years, the posts stood automatically created. The court also directed that the Rs 17,000 honorarium be implemented from 2017 itself. CM Yogi had announced in the Assembly on February 20 that instructors would receive Rs 17,000 instead of Rs 9,000. Proposal to increase salary passed in April In April, CM Yogi approved the proposal to increase salaries during a cabinet meeting. On April 9, Additional Chief Secretary Parth Sarathi Sen Sharma sent a copy of the order to the Director General of School Education.

stories.title: UP Evening Wrap:BSP risks losing national party status after poll setbacks;WHO declares global health emergency after Ebola outbreak more
stories.summary: Bhaskar English brings you the biggest news from Uttar Pradesh and around the world. Here are the top news headlines of the day- 1. Centre tells SC judge not mandatory in EC selection panel The Centre told the Supreme Court that there is no constitutional requirement to include a judge in the panel appointing the Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners. It said Parliament may include a judge as a policy choice, but it cannot be treated as a constitutional mandate. 2. Bulldozer drive outside Lucknow court sparks protest A demolition drive against illegal encroachments outside Lucknow District Court triggered protests by lawyers on Saturday. More than 100 advocates staged a sit-in as police deployed 300 personnel and six bulldozers to clear around 240 structures. 3. BSP risks losing national party status after poll setbacks The Bahujan Samaj Party may lose its national party status after failing to secure 1% vote share in West Bengal, Tamil Nadu and Kerala. The party also faces the possibility of losing representation in the Rajya Sabha. 4. Pakistan restores pre-partition names of localities in Lahore Pakistan has renamed several areas in Lahore, restoring their Hindu and British-era names after decades of Islamised identities. Nine localities have officially reverted to their original names within the past two months. 5. Severe heatwave grips UP, mercury nears 45°C in Banda Uttar Pradesh is witnessing intense heat conditions as temperatures approach 45°C in Banda and nearby regions. Authorities have issued heatwave alerts in 23 districts after rainfall and storms subsided across the state. 6. CM Yogi launches BJP training camp in Gorakhpur Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath inaugurated a BJP district training camp in Gorakhpur on Sunday. He said the BJP became the world’s largest political organisation in less than 50 years. 7. Centre tightens rules on silver imports The central government has imposed fresh restrictions on silver imports, making approval mandatory for several categories. The move was notified officially on Saturday as part of tighter import regulations. 8. Bulldozer action after salon manager suicide case in Lucknow Authorities demolished illegal construction at the apartment of the main accused in the Ratna Singh suicide case following CM Yogi Adityanath’s intervention. Police had earlier seized the accused businessman’s hotel, salon and three vehicles. 9. Maulana Madani alleges Muslims being intimidated in India Jamiat Ulema-e-Hind chief Maulana Arshad Madani alleged that Muslims are being threatened and Islam targeted in the country. He said the politics of fear and intimidation is prevailing, but Muslims “will not bow”. 10. WHO declares Ebola outbreak global health emergency The World Health Organisation has declared the Ebola outbreak in eastern DR Congo a global health emergency after 80 deaths and 246 suspected cases were reported. WHO clarified that the situation has not yet reached pandemic level.

stories.title: Four killed while returning from Bageshwar Dham:Car collides with truck in Hamirpur; three victims from same family
stories.summary: Four people, including a car driver, were killed after a WagonR car collided head-on with a truck in Hamirpur. Among the deceased, three belonged to the same family. All of them were returning to Kanpur after visiting Bageshwar Dham in Chhatarpur, Madhya Pradesh. The accident took place on Sunday afternoon near Chhirka village on National Highway-34 in the Maudaha Kotwali area. The collision was so severe that the WagonR was completely mangled. Even the seats inside the vehicle were uprooted due to the impact. All the occupants of the car were reportedly residents of Nawabganj in Kanpur. 3 members of same family among dead According to police, five people were travelling in the car. During an overtaking attempt, the WagonR collided with an oncoming truck. The deceased were identified as Narendra (55), Rajkapoor (57), his wife Meena (54), and driver Ayush Chauhan (25). 2 pictures of the accident- All four died on the spot Narendra’s wife Rekha (52) sustained serious injuries and was referred to Kanpur for treatment. Police said Narendra, Rajkapoor and Meena were residents of the Jageshwar Temple area in Nawabganj, Kanpur, while driver Ayush Chauhan was from Lucknow. Transport official witnessed the crash Satendra Singh, a Transport Corporation TI who was checking buses near the highway, said the WagonR had entered from the wrong side from the Mahoba direction and collided directly with the truck. He added that after the accident, one woman was still breathing when people reached the spot. Victims trapped inside car after crash Eyewitnesses said the car was travelling at nearly 80 kmph at the time of the accident. Both airbags deployed after the collision, but the impact severely damaged the vehicle. Several occupants became trapped inside the mangled car. Passersby informed the ambulance service and police, after which the injured were rescued from the vehicle with great difficulty.

stories.title: Maulana Arshad Madani alleges govt wants to harm Islam:Says Jamiat will go to court against Vande Mataram mandatory policy
stories.summary: Maulana Arshad Madani, president of Jamiat Ulema-e-Hind, has alleged that Islam is being targeted in the country and that Muslims are being intimidated and threatened. He said- Not only Muslims, but Islam itself is under attack. Madani claimed that politics based on hatred had now been replaced by politics driven by fear and intimidation. Attempts are being made to make Muslims feel that they will now have to live under certain conditions. Previous governments harmed Muslims, but the current government wants to harm Islam, he said. He made these remarks while addressing the two-day working committee session of Jamiat Ulema-e-Hind in Delhi. During the meeting, he also announced the formation of central and provincial madrasa boards to address issues related to madrasas. 1. Will move Court against giving Vande Mataram equal status Maulana Arshad Madani said granting Vande Mataram the same status as the national anthem Jana Gana Mana and making it mandatory in government and educational institutions was against the spirit of the Constitution and religious freedom. He said if the government did not withdraw the decision, Jamiat would approach the courts. Madani also said the organisation would continue its legal battle against the Uniform Civil Code (UCC). 2. Model Code violated in West Bengal and Assam Madani alleged that the Model Code of Conduct was openly violated during elections in West Bengal and Assam and claimed Muslims were publicly threatened. He said the trend had continued even after the elections. If a Chief Minister says Muslims did not vote for us, so we will not work for them, then it is an insult to both the Constitution and democracy 3. Government wants to harm Islam Madani reiterated that politics of hatred in the country had transformed into politics of fear and intimidation. He alleged that Muslims were being made to feel they would have to live under conditions imposed upon them. He said- Previous governments harmed Muslims, but the current government wants to harm Islam. 4- Muslims should keep documents safe Referring to the SIR process, Madani claimed it was not merely a voter list correction drive but a process similar to the NRC. He alleged that Muslims were being specifically targeted through it. He also described the declaration of 27 lakh voters as “suspicious” in West Bengal as a “black mark on democracy”. Madani urged Muslims to carefully fill out SIR forms and safely preserve all necessary documents. 5- Mosques, tombs and madrasas being demolished Madani alleged that mosques, tombs and madrasas were being demolished after being declared illegal. He said new orders against madrasas were continuously being issued. According to him, Jamiat Ulema-e-Hind was fighting legal battles against such actions and had received relief from courts in several cases. 6- Soviet Russia broke up but Islam survived Madani said those who attempted to erase Islam had themselves disappeared, while Islam continued to survive. Referring to the former Soviet Union, he said attempts had been made for years to eliminate Islam there, but ultimately the Soviet Union collapsed while Islam endured. He added that Indian Muslims were patriotic citizens and equal participants in the country’s progress. He said- Muslims have proved their patriotism in every difficult period.

stories.title: Uttar Pradesh CM launches BJP training camp in Gorakhpur:Yogi Adityanath says party became world’s largest political organisation in less than 50 years
stories.summary: Yogi Adityanath inaugurated the BJP District Training Camp in Gorakhpur on Sunday. The programme was organised at a resort in the Sahjanwa Assembly constituency as part of the two-day training session being held on May 17 and 18. Addressing party workers, the Chief Minister said the Bharatiya Janata Party had become the world’s largest political party within less than 50 years of its formation. He said the BJP had independently formed governments at the Centre and in 22 states across the country. ‘Nation first, party second, individual last’ Yogi Adityanath said the BJP was the only political party in the country and the world that had consistently upheld the principle of “Nation first, party second and individual interest last”. He said the party had always worked with nationalism as its core ideology. See 5 pictures CM recalls sacrifice of Syama Prasad Mookerjee The Chief Minister said Syama Prasad Mookerjee had entered Kashmir to protest against the permit system along with his associates. According to Yogi Adityanath, Mookerjee was arrested and later died in a Jammu and Kashmir jail. He said the sacrifice of leaders who fought for the country helped strengthen the foundation of the Bharatiya Jana Sangh. Tribute to Deendayal Upadhyaya The Chief Minister also remembered Deendayal Upadhyaya, saying he advocated ensuring that government welfare schemes reached even the last person in society. He said Upadhyaya later became president of the Bharatiya Jana Sangh and also faced betrayal and an untimely death. According to Yogi Adityanath, Upadhyaya understood that political stability was essential for development and worked continuously towards strengthening the organisation. BJP’s political journey explained The Chief Minister said the credit for the formation of the first non-Congress government in 1967 also went to Deendayal Upadhyaya. He said the Bharatiya Jana Sangh later entered a new phase under Atal Bihari Vajpayee and Lal Krishna Advani. During that period, the Bharatiya Jana Sangh merged with the Janata Party to strengthen the democracy movement. He said the BJP was later formed on April 6, 1980, under the leadership of Atal Bihari Vajpayee. He further said- The BJP had won only two MPs initially. Today, it has become the world’s largest political party. ‘BJP workers must remain different from other parties’ Yogi Adityanath urged BJP workers to uphold the party’s values and ideals in their personal conduct. He said if BJP workers began behaving like leaders and workers of parties such as the Congress, SP, BSP, RJD, TMC and DMK, society would never respect them. According to him, BJP workers must function differently while respecting India and Indian values. He also stressed the need to strengthen the BJP organisation through better coordination and strong booth-level structures. He also said- Our booth should remain our central focus. ‘BJP gave women the Right to Live with dignity’ The Chief Minister said the BJP had supported the construction of the Ram Temple in Ayodhya in 1986 as part of its commitment to cultural nationalism. He said a grand Ram Temple had now been constructed under the double-engine government. According to him, India had emerged as a beacon of hope globally. He also said the BJP had given women the right to live with dignity by banning the practice of triple talaq. Yogi Adityanath added that reservation for women in Parliament and state assemblies through the Women’s Reservation Act had been introduced under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. 2-day training camp and Janata Darshan The BJP District Training Camp will continue for two days on May 17 and 18. As mobile phones were prohibited during the programme, BJP workers deposited their phones at Assembly-wise counters set up at the venue. Before attending the event, Yogi Adityanath also heard grievances of around 150 people during the Janata Darshan programme organised at Gorakhnath Temple.

stories.title: Woman manager suicide case — Action after CM Yogi’s intervention:Accused businessman’s friend arrested, apartment demolished ; hotel and 3 cars seized
stories.summary: Police on Sunday arrested businessman Sharad Singh and his friend Prashant Sharma, the main accused in the suicide case of salon manager Ratna Singh (31) in Lucknow’s Gomtinagar Extension area. A day earlier, authorities had carried out bulldozer action at Sharad Singh’s apartment and demolished alleged illegal constructions on the premises. His hotel, salon and three cars were also seized as part of the action. Ratna, who worked as a manager at businessman Sharad Singh’s salon, died by suicide on May 12 by hanging herself. Before taking the step, she recorded a video accusing businessman Sharad Singh, his wife Pallavi Singh and several others of harassment. Ratna’s father, Sudhir Singh, later lodged a named FIR against five people. Father met CM Yogi over delay in action Alleging inaction by the police, Sudhir Singh met Yogi Adityanath on May 15. On May 16, he released a video claiming that Sharad Singh was evading arrest by using his influence. He alleged that despite registration of the case, the police had failed to take concrete action. Sudhir said he had appealed to the Chief Minister for justice and was assured that strict action would be taken. Following the meeting with the Chief Minister, action in the case intensified. Police announced a reward of Rs 25,000 each on the accused and formed six teams to trace them. Raids are currently underway in Lucknow and several other districts. 5 pictures of police action Ratna recorded video before suicide Ratna Singh, a resident of Gorakhpur, died by suicide on May 12 in Shalimar Vista Apartment in Gomtinagar Extension after recording a video message. In the video, she made serious allegations against businessman Sharad Singh, his wife, along with Mangal Yadav, Vaishali and Prashant Sharma. Based on a complaint filed by her father Sudhir Singh, Gomtinagar Extension police registered a case against the accused. Within 24 hours, police arrested only one accused, Mangalnath Yadav, who reportedly worked at Sharad Singh’s hotel. Father Accuses Police of Negligence In the video released on May 16, Sudhir Singh said his daughter worked at Virasat Company in Lucknow and had named Sharad Singh and his associates before ending her life. According to him, Ratna had alleged physical and mental harassment by the accused, which drove her to suicide. Sudhir said- A case was registered on May 12 against the named accused, but so far only one arrest has been made. On the evening of May 15, I met Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, who assured me that justice would be delivered and strict action would be taken. I have faith in the justice system. May 16 has passed, now let us see what happens next See the pictures of the accused- ‘She was harassed for opposing wrongdoing’ Sudhir Singh alleged that his daughter had come to know about the “dark activities” of accused Sharad Singh and began facing harassment after opposing them. He claimed Ratna did not support the alleged illegal activities being carried out under the guise of the hotel business. “She was very brave, but eventually broke down. To stop the matter from reaching the family, she chose death,” he alleged. He further claimed that negligence by the police allowed Sharad Singh and the other accused to escape. Two major actions taken after complaint to CM DCP East Dr Diksha Sharma said - A reward of Rs 25,000 each had been announced for the absconding accused. Six police teams, including surveillance units, have been formed to arrest them, and raids are being conducted in Lucknow and other districts. All the accused will be in police custody soon.

stories.title: Bulldozer action sparks protest outside Lucknow court:Scuffle breaks out between police and lawyers; 6 bulldozers, 300 policemen deployed
stories.summary: A demolition drive against illegal encroachments began outside the Lucknow District Court at 9 am on Saturday. Around 240 illegal structures, including lawyers’ chambers and roadside shops, are being demolished using six bulldozers. As the administration’s team arrived with bulldozers in the morning, more than 100 lawyers gathered at the site. They raised slogans and staged a sit-in protest by sitting on the ground. Scuffle breaks out during protest When police attempted to remove the protesters, an argument broke out between the police, lawyers and shopkeepers. The situation soon escalated into pushing and shoving. Police later used batons to disperse the protesting lawyers and shopkeepers from the area. At present, four ACPs, personnel from the Provincial Armed Constabulary (PAC), and more than 300 police personnel have been deployed at the spot. Encroachments had occupied roads, footpaths and drains According to the administration, lawyers’ chambers and photocopy shops had been constructed illegally by occupying roads, footpaths and drainage areas, causing inconvenience to commuters. The matter had reached the Allahabad High Court, following which the court ordered the removal of illegal encroachments. The municipal corporation later issued notices directing occupants to remove the encroachments. While some people voluntarily cleared the structures, a large number failed to comply, leading to the demolition action. See photos-
