stories.title: Will BSP lose its national party status?:Fails to secure 1% votes in Bengal, Tamil Nadu and Kerala; may lose Rajya Sabha presence too
stories.summary: There are currently six national parties in the country, BJP, Indian National Congress (Congress), Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP), Communist Party of India (Marxist) (CPI-M), Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) and National People's Party (NPP). However, BSP’s status as a national party is now under serious threat. The party failed to secure even 1% of the vote share in the Assembly elections in West Bengal, Tamil Nadu and Kerala. BSP also has no representation in the Lok Sabha and only one MP in the Rajya Sabha. The key question now is how serious the threat to BSP’s national party status has become, why the party has managed to retain recognition so far, and why the upcoming Assembly elections in Uttar Pradesh, Punjab and Uttarakhand are crucial for its survival. Poor performance in Bengal, Kerala and Tamil Nadu BSP fielded candidates on 152 out of 294 seats in the West Bengal Assembly elections, but all candidates forfeited their deposits. The party secured only 1.17 lakh votes, accounting for 0.18% of the total vote share. In Kerala, where Assembly elections were held on 140 seats, BSP contested 55 constituencies. The party received only 33,125 votes, or 0.15% of the vote share. Similarly, in Tamil Nadu, BSP fielded candidates on 118 out of 234 Assembly seats and managed just 53,369 votes, equivalent to 0.11% of the vote share. Across all three states combined, BSP received only 2.04 lakh votes, failing to meet the criteria required for recognition as a state party in any of them. BSP opened account in Bihar, but vote share stayed below 2% In the 2025 Bihar Assembly elections, BSP contested 192 out of 243 seats. The party managed to win only one seat and secured a total of 8.13 lakh votes, translating to 1.62% vote share. Despite opening its account in the state, BSP still failed to fulfil the criteria required for recognition as a state party in Bihar. Weak performance in Delhi, Haryana, Maharashtra and Jharkhand Delhi In the February 2025 Delhi Assembly elections, BSP contested 68 out of 70 seats. None of its candidates managed to save their deposits. The party received around 55,000 votes, or 0.58% vote share. Haryana During the October 2024 Haryana Assembly elections, BSP contested in alliance with Indian National Lok Dal (INLD). The party fielded candidates on 35 out of 90 seats, but all lost their deposits. BSP secured 2.52 lakh votes, amounting to 1.82% vote share. Maharashtra In the November 2024 Maharashtra Assembly elections, BSP contested 237 out of 288 seats. All candidates forfeited their deposits, while the party’s vote share stood at just 0.48%. Jharkhand BSP fielded candidates on all 81 Assembly seats in the 2024 Jharkhand elections held between November and December. The party failed to win a single seat, and its vote share remained below 1%. BSP had earlier saved its national party status in 2014 BSP was granted national party status in 1997. However, in 2014, the party came close to losing this recognition after failing to win a single Lok Sabha seat. Its national vote share had also dropped to 4.19%. In August 2014, the Election Commission issued show-cause notices to BSP, Nationalist Congress Party (NCP) and Communist Party of India (CPI), asking why their national party status should not be revoked. BSP then sought additional time from the Election Commission and requested that the review be deferred until after the Delhi Assembly election results. In 2016, the Election Commission amended the Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968. Under the revised rules, the review process for national parties, which earlier took place every five years, was extended to once every 10 years. The amendment provided temporary relief to BSP, NCP and CPI until 2019. Later, BSP managed to secure more than 6% vote share in Assembly elections in Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Rajasthan, Bihar and Punjab. This helped the party retain its recognition as a state party in multiple states and, in turn, preserve its national party status.

stories.title: UP braces for severe heatwave:Temperature nears 45°C in Banda, alert in 23 districts
stories.summary: As storms and rain subsided across Uttar Pradesh, intense heat returned to the state, with temperatures nearing 45°C. The sky remained clear in most cities from Sunday morning, while bright sunshine and low wind speed increased humidity levels. The Meteorological Department has issued a heatwave alert for 23 cities today. Rising daytime temperatures are expected to intensify the heat, with temperatures likely to continue increasing over the next five days. From May 20 onwards, the heatwave is expected to become more severe, affecting more than half of the state’s cities. No rainfall was recorded anywhere in the state during the past 24 hours. Banda remained the hottest city for the fifth consecutive day, recording a maximum temperature of 44.8°C. Bijnor was the coolest city, where the minimum temperature settled at 20.2°C. Lucknow meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh said- The monsoon is expected to reach Kerala around May 26. Based on current estimates, it may enter Uttar Pradesh through Gorakhpur around June 18. However, this is only a probable date. The exact timeline will be assessed after the monsoon advances from Kerala. At present, there is no immediate relief from the heat. The entire state will remain under severe heat conditions for at least the next week. See photos- Weather forecast for the next 5 days May 18- Strong sunshine is expected across East and West UP. Heatwave conditions may prevail during the afternoon, while winds could blow at speeds of 20–30 kmph. May 19- Light cloud cover may appear in some areas, but no rainfall is expected. Heatwave conditions are likely during the afternoon. May 20- The weather will remain dry in West UP, with no storm or rain alert. Some areas of East UP may receive light rainfall. May 21- Light showers may occur in parts of north-eastern Purvanchal, while severe heat will continue across West UP. May 22- The weather is expected to remain clear in West UP, where heatwave conditions will persist. Some eastern districts may receive light rain. Weather conditions in major cities Lucknow Bright sunshine and clear skies have prevailed since morning, accompanied by hot winds. The maximum temperature is expected to reach 41°C, while the minimum may remain around 27°C. Intense heat is also likely during the night. Kanpur Strong sunshine has continued since morning, and a heatwave alert has been issued for the afternoon. People stepping outdoors were seen covering their faces with cloth, gamchas and angocchas. No relief from the heat is expected for at least a week. Gorakhpur Temperatures are rising due to strong sunshine and westerly winds. Roads witnessed thinner crowds during the day. Intense sunshine is expected to trouble residents, while humid conditions may continue at night. Meerut The weather has remained clear since morning with bright sunshine. For the first time this May, the temperature may cross 40°C. Morning temperatures were already recorded above 30°C, while wind speeds could remain around 10–12 kmph. Ghaziabad Bright sunshine has prevailed since morning, with severe heat expected during the day. The temperature was recorded at 29°C in the early morning, while the maximum may touch 40.8°C later in the day. Wind speed is expected to remain around 10 kmph. UP likely to receive below-normal monsoon rainfall The Meteorological Department has predicted below-normal rainfall in Uttar Pradesh between June and September. India Meteorological Department Director General Dr M. Mohapatra said weather conditions resembling La Niña in the Pacific Ocean are now showing signs of shifting towards El Niño conditions, which could reduce rainfall. This indicates that the southwest monsoon may remain weaker than normal this year. He added that low snow cover in the Northern Hemisphere between January and March could also affect the monsoon. Last year’s monsoon was 10–15% above normal According to the Meteorological Department, Uttar Pradesh received an average rainfall of 870–900 mm during the 2025 monsoon season between June and September. This was around 10–15% higher than the normal monsoon average. Crops damaged by storms and rain; Yogi assures support Heavy rain and storms on Wednesday and Thursday caused widespread damage to crops across the state. Vegetable crops such as cucumber, gherkin and watermelon were among the worst affected. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath said on Thursday that the government stands with farmers and the public during this difficult period. He said authorities are continuously monitoring the situation to ensure timely assistance reaches those in need, and warned that negligence by officials during relief operations would not be tolerated. Why is the weather fluctuating? According to the Meteorological Department, weather conditions in the hills of Uttarakhand have been changing continuously, with snowfall in some areas and rainfall in others. On certain days, the weather clears with strong sunshine. Similar fluctuations are expected to continue over the next few days, affecting Uttar Pradesh as well. Winds blowing from the hills have helped keep temperatures comparatively lower at times and are also creating conditions favourable for rainfall.

stories.title: 111 dead as violent storms batter Uttar Pradesh:From AC blasts to sudden daytime darkness, extreme weather shocks residents across several districts
stories.summary: From people being thrown by violent winds to air-conditioners exploding in scorching heat and cities turning dark in the middle of the morning, Uttar Pradesh has witnessed a series of extreme weather events over the past few weeks. After unseasonal rain and storms, temperatures are now expected to climb again to 45°C–47°C by the end of May. At the same time, meteorologists say the monsoon could arrive nearly a week earlier than usual. However, despite the intense heat, monsoon rains are coming 7 days earlier to provide relief to people this time. The monsoon will enter UP by June 18. Why is the weather changing so rapidly in UP, find out in Sunday Big Story Three incidents that shocked Uttar Pradesh Man blown nearly 100 metres during storm On May 13, winds blowing at nearly 90 kmph struck Bareilly. During the storm, a man was reportedly lifted almost 50 feet into the air and thrown nearly 100 metres into a maize field. He suffered fractures in one arm and one leg. Multiple AC explosions amid extreme heat Between April and May, at least six buildings in Noida and Ghaziabad reported air-conditioner explosions. Officials and technicians believe the compressors failed because they could not withstand temperatures touching 45°C. Daytime turned into ‘night’ in Lucknow On the morning of May 4, Lucknow witnessed sudden darkness around 9 am despite clear weather earlier in the day. Drivers were forced to switch on headlights as thick clouds covered the city. Heavy rain and strong winds followed shortly afterward. Uttar Pradesh witnessing extreme temperature swings Meteorologists say Uttar Pradesh has experienced both record-breaking heat and sudden weather reversals this season. 37 UP cities among world’s hottest On April 23, 92 Indian cities featured among the world’s 100 hottest locations, including 37 from Uttar Pradesh. After Maharashtra’s Khed district, the hottest places included Mughalsarai, Amethi, Varanasi and Ghazipur in Uttar Pradesh. On April 27, Banda recorded 47.6°C, making it the hottest place in the world that day. Districts including Prayagraj, Chitrakoot and Hamirpur also recorded temperatures above 45°C for several consecutive days. Residents feared May and June would become unbearable. Sudden shift from heatwave to rainstorms However, the expected escalation in heat did not happen immediately. In the first week of May, temperatures suddenly dropped as rainfall began in western Uttar Pradesh before spreading across the state. On May 4 and 5, almost every district in Uttar Pradesh received rain. The state recorded 27.4 mm rainfall during the first week of May — nearly seven times higher than the average May rainfall of 3.3 mm. Then, on May 13, violent storms and strong winds killed 111 people across the state. Officials said it was the highest single-day death toll caused by weather-related incidents in the past decade. Prayagraj reported 21 deaths, while Bhadohi recorded 17 fatalities. The deaths even drew condolences from Russian President Vladimir Putin. Why is the weather changing so rapidly? Scientists say the dramatic weather swings are being driven by atmospheric instability caused by the collision of cold and warm air systems. Cold air above, hot air below Dr. Atul Singh, senior scientist at the Regional Meteorological Centre in Lucknow, explained that western disturbances were pushing dry and cold winds across the upper atmosphere. At the same time, warm and moisture-laden winds were moving from the east at lower atmospheric levels. Clash of air masses triggered instability When cold, dry air collided with warm, humid air, the atmosphere became unstable. Meteorologists say this instability intensified because a cyclonic circulation had already formed over western Uttar Pradesh. As hot air rose rapidly and collided with colder air above, it triggered violent thunderstorms, lightning and powerful windstorms. Scientists say this explains why storms became so intense in places like Bareilly and why cities like Lucknow experienced sudden daytime darkness. Have such storms happened before? According to scientists, Uttar Pradesh has experienced major storms in previous years as well, particularly in 2016, 2018 and 2020. However, this year’s storms were unusually intense because wind speeds were significantly higher. Earlier storms typically recorded wind speeds between 60 and 80 kmph. This year, several regions witnessed speeds crossing 100 kmph. Meteorologists say wind intensity also depends on local geographical conditions, which is why one part of a district may record 110 kmph winds while another area experiences much lower speeds. They describe the current phase as a “pre-monsoon season,” though weather patterns this year are shifting much faster than usual. What is El Niño and why does it matter? Scientists believe another major reason behind the unusual weather is the warming of the Pacific Ocean, known as El Niño. El Niño refers to changes in sea surface temperatures in the Pacific Ocean. This year, the eastern and central Pacific are significantly warmer than normal, with water temperatures reportedly touching 24°C. Meteorologists say when ocean temperatures rise sharply, weather patterns across India become unstable. This can result in both severe heatwaves and sudden storms or rainfall. However, scientists stress that El Niño alone does not control the monsoon. Several other atmospheric and oceanic factors also influence India’s weather system. Monsoon likely to arrive early Despite fears of extreme heat, meteorologists believe the monsoon may arrive earlier than expected. Arabian Sea and Bay of Bengal playing key role Scientists say the Arabian Sea and Bay of Bengal are currently warmer than normal, creating large amounts of moisture. This has made monsoon winds “super active,” allowing the monsoon system to advance rapidly. Normally, the monsoon reaches Kerala around June 1. This year, it is expected to arrive by May 26 — nearly four days early. Uttar Pradesh could get monsoon by June 18 Weather experts now estimate that the monsoon could reach Uttar Pradesh by June 18. Earlier forecasts had suggested people in the state might have to wait until early July. Concern over weak monsoon and heatwaves The US weather agency National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) has warned that a “super El Niño” is likely this year. Meteorologists fear this could weaken overall monsoon rainfall while increasing the risks of drought and prolonged heatwaves. What lies ahead? The India Meteorological Department has warned that intense heat is likely to return over the next 10 days. Districts such as Prayagraj, Banda and Chitrakoot are expected to see temperatures once again cross 45°C. Western Uttar Pradesh is also likely to experience severe heat conditions.

stories.title: Lucknow civic body to administer oath to councillor Lalit Tiwari:Municipal commissioner calls councillor after legal opinion
stories.summary: The Lucknow Municipal Corporation will administer the oath of office to Samajwadi Party councillor Lalit Kishore Tiwari on Sunday. The swearing-in ceremony has been scheduled for 9 am at the civic body's headquarters in Lalbagh. Lalit Tiwari has been informed through an official letter issued by the committee department. Following the High Court’s order, the Municipal Corporation had sought legal advice from its legal adviser. The opinion recommended that Tiwari be administered the oath without delay. According to information received, Mayor Sushma Kharkwal was discharged from Command Hospital on Saturday afternoon. After her discharge, instructions were issued to ensure that the oath ceremony takes place under all circumstances. Legal Adviser Tells Municipal Commissioner to Ensure Early Oath Ceremony Following the High Court order, Lucknow Municipal Corporation’s legal adviser Prashant Singh Atal submitted his legal opinion to Municipal Commissioner Gaurav Kumar, advising immediate compliance with the court’s directions. Singh stated that, as per the law, petitioner Lalit Tiwari should be administered the oath at the earliest. He further advised that, after the oath ceremony, a compliance affidavit should be filed before the High Court informing it that the order has been implemented. According to the legal opinion, once the court’s directions are complied with, the Mayor’s financial and administrative powers will be restored. Municipal Commissioner Summons Lalit Tiwari Municipal Commissioner Gaurav Kumar had called court-declared councillor Lalit Tiwari to the Smart City office on Saturday for a meeting. However, Tiwari informed officials that he was in Kanpur and said he would be available to meet later in the evening.

stories.title: Uncle, nephew killed after CO’s vehicle hits bike in Lakhimpur:Motorcycle thrown 3 feet into air after collision with Bolero
stories.summary: An uncle and nephew were killed after being run over by the official Bolero vehicle of a Circle Officer (CO) in Uttar Pradesh’s Lakhimpur Kheri district. Both were travelling on a motorcycle when the accident occurred. The impact was so severe that the motorcycle was thrown nearly three feet into the air. Both victims fell headfirst onto the road. The uncle died on the spot. At the time of the accident, Mohammadi CO Arun Kumar Singh was reportedly travelling in the vehicle. Passersby at the scene rushed the nephew to hospital, where he later succumbed to his injuries during treatment. After being informed by police, family members reached the hospital. During questioning, they told police that the uncle and nephew were on their way to the town to purchase agricultural medicine. The incident took place in the Mohammadi police station area, around 70 km from the district headquarters. See 2 pictures of the incident site CO was going to attend Thana Diwas CO Arun Kumar Singh was travelling in a government Bolero from Mohammadi to Pasgawan, around 8 km away, to attend a Thana Diwas programme. At around noon, the Bolero collided with a motorcycle on the Mohammadi-Kandharapur road. The motorcycle was carrying Jayram (50) and his nephew Ram Avtar (45). The collision was so powerful that both men were thrown off the motorcycle and landed headfirst on the road. People present at the spot rushed them to the Mohammadi Community Health Centre for treatment. Doctors declared Jayram dead on arrival, while Ram Avtar died during treatment. Hospital turned into a camp after news of commotion As news of the accident spread, Ram Avtar’s wife Reshma and other family members were left devastated. The family reached the hospital and began protesting. Sensing tension, Mohammadi SDM, Tehsildar Arun Kumar, the local inspector and a large police force arrived at the hospital. Officials managed to calm the grieving family after considerable effort. Ram Avtar used to do farming while living at his in-laws' place The uncle and nephew were residents of Anaya village in Shahjahanpur district. Ram Avtar’s in-laws live in Pihani under Raigai police station limits. He had been living there and working as a farmer. He was travelling to Mohammadi with his uncle to purchase medicines for farming. Jayram was unmarried and was also engaged in agricultural work. Police have sent both bodies for post-mortem examination. The CO’s Bolero has been parked at Mohammadi police station. Police officials said the circumstances leading to the accident are being investigated. Action will be taken based on eyewitness statements and evidence collected from the scene. Son of deceased filed complaint against CO Anuj, son of deceased Ram Avtar, has submitted a complaint against Mohammadi CO Arun Kumar Singh. In the complaint, he alleged that the government vehicle was being driven at high speed and negligently by the driver while the CO was present in the vehicle. People present at the scene also claimed that the driver appeared to be intoxicated and was unable to speak properly. Responding to the allegations, CO Arun Singh said: “I was travelling with the police team for Thana Diwas. A speeding motorcycle came from the opposite direction and hit the Bolero. Two people died in the accident. Our driver also sustained injuries.” SP Dr Khyati Garg said: “Two people have died in the accident. The post-mortem examination is being conducted. The matter is being investigated. The family has submitted a complaint. Appropriate action will be taken.”

stories.title: UP panchayat polls only after Assembly elections:Proposal sent to Yogi; administrators likely in villages from May 26
stories.summary: Speculation surrounding the Uttar Pradesh panchayat elections has finally come to an end. The elections are now expected to be held only after the 2027 Assembly polls. The tenure of village heads in the state's 57,695 gram panchayats is ending in three days, on May 26. In view of this, the Panchayati Raj Department has sent a proposal to the Chief Minister seeking the appointment of administrators in villages after the tenure of elected village heads ends. However, Panchayati Raj Minister Om Prakash Rajbhar said that no order has been issued yet. He confirmed that the proposal has been sent to the Chief Minister for approval. A few days ago, the Panchayati Raj Department had also sent a proposal to the Cabinet seeking either the appointment of administrators or the formation of administrative committees to manage village affairs after the term of gram pradhans expires. Department Director Amit Singh had said: There is no provision to extend the tenure of Gram Pradhans. An administrator will be appointed at the government level. There is a provision to appoint the 'Gram Panchayat Assistant' of panchayats as 'Administrator'. Until elections are held, the administrator handles the work of the Gram Panchayat. Why will administrators be appointed... 1. Final voter list not yet published The final publication of the voter list for panchayat elections has not taken place yet. While the term of village heads ends on May 26, the final electoral roll will be published only on June 10. 2. OBC reservation process still pending The Cabinet has already approved a proposal to constitute an OBC Commission to determine reservation for Other Backward Classes in panchayat elections. The commission is expected to submit its report within three to six months of its formation. Only after that will reservation categories for the elections be finalised. The entire process could take around six months. 3. Government considering polls after Assembly elections The government is considering holding panchayat elections after the 2027 Assembly elections. Political parties are also broadly in agreement with the idea, though the matter is currently under consideration before the Allahabad High Court. Pradhan Sangh had demanded formation of 'Administrative Committee' Dainik Bhaskar had earlier spoken to Akhilesh Singh, National President of the National Panchayati Raj Gram Pradhan Organisation, on the issue. He said a delegation of the organisation met Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on April 20 and demanded the formation of administrative committees. The same demand was later placed before BJP state president Pankaj Chaudhary during a meeting on May 16. Organisation Vice-President Lalit Kumar Sharma had said that if panchayat elections are not conducted on time, the state government or district magistrate can appoint an administrator or form an administrative committee. This can be done under Section 12(3A) of the Panchayati Raj Act, 1947. Under such a system, the administrative committee includes a gram pradhan or a chairperson nominated by the government. Ward members, the gram pradhan and the village panchayat assistant can also be made members of the committee. Difficulties arise from appointing administrators National President Akhilesh Singh had pointed out that appointing government employees as administrators in gram panchayats often creates several difficulties for villagers.

stories.title: UP Evening Wrap:7 arrested for cheating in SSC online exam; India looking to buy oil from US amid Hormuz blockage more
stories.summary: Bhaskar English brings you the biggest news from Madhya Pradesh and around the world. Here are the top news headlines of the day: 1. India looking to buy oil from US amid Hormuz blockage Iran has warned of a “crushing” response if the United States launches fresh military strikes, while reports suggest Washington is weighing military options despite ongoing diplomatic efforts. Iran has temporarily closed parts of its western airspace amid security concerns, as tensions around the strategically important Strait of Hormuz continue to fuel global energy market uncertainty. 2. 7 arrested for cheating in SSC online exam UP STF raided a Greater Noida examination centre and arrested seven people, including the alleged mastermind, for rigging SSC recruitment exams through a proxy server network. Officials recovered ₹50 lakh cash, laptops and mobile phones. Candidates were allegedly charged up to ₹4 lakh to pass exams. 3. BJP MLA Nand Kishore Gurjar claims cockroach Janata Party a foreign force BJP MLA Nand Kishore Gurjar termed the so-called "Cockroach Janata Party" a foreign-backed conspiracy aimed at disturbing the country's atmosphere. He alleged links with foreign funding, opposition parties and people with a jihadist mindset, claiming efforts were being made to create social unrest and caste tensions. Gurjar said he would write to Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath seeking action against those involved. 4. Fuel price hiked again, 3rd increase in 10 days Petrol and diesel prices have been raised for the third time in less than 10 days, with petrol becoming costlier by 87 paise per litre and diesel by 91 paise. CNG prices have also increased by ₹1 per kg. The hike comes amid rising global crude oil prices linked to tensions in West Asia, pushing fuel rates up by nearly ₹5 per litre since May 15. 5. 4 dead, 1 critical as dumper runs over family sleeping outside in Barabanki Four members of a family, including three children, were killed after an out-of-control dumper truck ran over them while they were sleeping outside their home during a power outage in Uttar Pradesh's Barabanki district. The children's mother was critically injured, while the driver fled the scene after abandoning the vehicle. 6. Influencer student assaulted at Kashi Vidyapeeth after ‘fat’ remark A social media influencer and student of Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith in Varanasi was allegedly chased, dragged to the ground and beaten by two female classmates after an argument following an exam. The victim claimed the assault was part of a conspiracy to defame her. Police said no formal complaint has been filed yet and the matter is being examined. 7. 90 killed in massive coal mine explosion in China More than 90 workers were killed and dozens remained trapped after a gas explosion ripped through a coal mine in China's Shanxi province on Friday night. President Xi Jinping ordered full-scale rescue operations and a thorough investigation, while officials vowed strict action against those found responsible for the deadly accident. 8. OP officers approach RSS, BJP offices to get transfers With Uttar Pradesh's final major transfer exercise before the 2027 Assembly elections underway, officers and employees are lobbying for preferred postings through ministers, BJP leaders and RSS functionaries. Transfer lists are expected by May 31, with the government retaining a 20% cap on transfers for Group A and B officers. 9. Azam Khan, son Abdullah get 10-year jail term in fake PAN case A Rampur MP/MLA court has enhanced the sentence of Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan and his son Abdullah Azam Khan from seven to 10 years in the fake PAN card case. The court also imposed a fine of ₹5 lakh on each after accepting the Uttar Pradesh government's plea for a harsher punishment, citing misuse of forged identity documents and fraud. 10. SpaceX rocket explodes in the Indian Ocean after splashdown Elon Musk's SpaceX successfully launched the first test flight of its upgraded Starship V3 rocket, the largest and most powerful rocket ever built. The mission lasted about an hour before the spacecraft carried out a planned splashdown in the Indian Ocean, where it exploded as intended. Despite engine failures in both stages, the test achieved most of its key objectives, marking another milestone in the Starship programme.

stories.title: FIR against Ajay Rai over remarks on PM Modi:Says he is being harassed; booked under multiple charges
stories.summary: An FIR has been registered against Uttar Pradesh Congress president Ajay Rai over alleged abusive remarks against Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Based on a complaint filed by BJP district working committee member Neeraj Kumar Rawat in Mahoba, a case has been registered against Ajay Rai and 30 others. The complaint accuses them of spreading hatred, gathering a crowd without permission, obstructing government work and blocking a public road. The controversy erupted after Ajay Rai allegedly evaded police surveillance on Friday and reached Mahoba to meet a NEET student who claims she was a victim of gang rape and abduction. After meeting the student, Rai was sitting in his car preparing to leave when he allegedly used abusive language against Prime Minister Modi, Mahoba SP Shashank Singh and the officer’s mother while speaking to a party worker. The conversation was reportedly captured on camera. After the video surfaced, political tensions escalated sharply. Senior BJP leaders launched a strong attack on Ajay Rai and the Congress party. However, Rai dismissed the clip, claiming it was AI-generated. Ajay Rai said: I visited Mahoba because a Dalit girl was allegedly raped for 16 days. She was injected with intoxicants and burned with cigarettes. When I raised her issue, it did not go down well with the BJP. Cases are being filed against me through AI-generated videos. I am being harassed. I want to tell the government that it can file not one but 100 cases against me, but it should ensure justice for that Dalit girl. I am ready to go to jail. See 2 pictures First read what complaint was made against Ajay Rai... In his written complaint submitted at Mahoba Kotwali police station, Neeraj Rawat alleged that Congress secretary Brajraj Ahirwar invited Ajay Rai to the house of Rajkumar Ahirwar, a resident of his locality, without administrative permission. According to the complaint, the Congress leader arrived with 25-26 supporters in a convoy of 15-16 vehicles. The vehicles were allegedly parked haphazardly, blocking a public road. Officials responsible for maintaining law and order reportedly had to leave their duties and rush to the location. The complaint further alleged that the Congress leader made abusive remarks against Prime Minister Modi and that a video of the incident had gone viral. The BJP leader submitted the video clip to the police and demanded registration of an FIR. ASP Vandana Singh stated- On May 22, 2026, a video was received through social media. In which Ajay Rai along with his supporters disrupted government work. Traffic was jammed on a public road. Indecent comments were also made against the Prime Minister. A complaint was received in Mahoba regarding the video, under which a case was registered. Legal action is being taken in the matter as per law. stories.title: Azam Khan, son Abdullah get 3-year sentence hike:Court accepts plea for enhanced punishment; both to remain in jail for 10 years
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan and his son Abdullah Azam Khan will now have to serve 10 years in prison. On Saturday, the Rampur MP/MLA Court increased their seven-year sentence in the fake PAN card case by another three years each. The court also imposed a fine of ₹5 lakh on both of them. On November 17, 2025, the same MP/MLA Court had sentenced Azam and Abdullah to seven years in jail and imposed a fine of ₹50,000 each. Both have been lodged in Rampur Jail since then. Meanwhile, on May 5, 2026, Additional District Government Counsel (ADGC) Seema Rana filed an appeal on behalf of the Uttar Pradesh government seeking enhancement of the sentence. Her argument was that the case was not merely about irregularities in documents but involved the misuse of government identity documents and serious fraud. Therefore, both should be awarded life imprisonment. Just a week ago, the Rampur MP/MLA Court had also sentenced Azam Khan to two years in jail over his “Collector-Flector Tankhaiya” remark. BJP MLA who filed FIR says - I am happy with the decision Rampur BJP MLA Akash Saxena had lodged a case at Civil Lines police station in 2019, accusing Abdullah of possessing two PAN cards. After investigation, police also added Azam Khan’s name to the case. Reacting to the verdict, Akash Saxena said, “This is a historic judgment. For the first time in India, a sentence in such a case has been enhanced. I had requested the court to award the maximum punishment. The court increased the sentence, and I am happy with the decision.” Government lawyer Seema Rana said: “The court has delivered its verdict on the government’s appeal seeking enhancement of punishment in the two-PAN-card case. Although we had sought life imprisonment, the court has increased the sentence by three years each. We are satisfied with the decision. Azam and Abdullah kept making mistake after mistake Azam Khan served as Urban Development Minister in the Akhilesh Yadav government in 2017. During the Assembly elections, he wanted his son Abdullah to contest from the Swar seat in Rampur. However, Abdullah was underage according to his educational records. As per his actual date of birth—January 1, 1993—Abdullah was not eligible to contest the 2017 Assembly election because he had not yet turned 25. Using his influence, Azam allegedly got a fake birth certificate issued for his son from the Lucknow Municipal Corporation. In the certificate, Abdullah’s birth year was shown as 1990. Based on this document, Abdullah allegedly obtained fake PAN cards and continued using the incorrect details repeatedly. When the 2017 Assembly elections were held, Abdullah won the Swar seat. However, former BSP candidate Nawab Kazim Ali Khan raised the issue of fake PAN cards and claimed Abdullah was below 25 years of age at the time of nomination. An inquiry later found that Abdullah had contested the election using a false age certificate and was not eligible to contest. His election was subsequently declared void and he lost his Assembly membership. In this case, BJP leader Akash Saxena also filed a complaint in Rampur on July 30, 2019. He alleged that Abdullah Azam had obtained two PAN cards in violation of rules. The case eventually led to jail terms not only for Abdullah but also for his father Azam Khan and mother Tanzeen Fatima. However, Abdullah won the Swar Assembly seat again in the 2022 elections. Later, he was sentenced to more than three years in another case related to obstructing government work, leading to the cancellation of his Assembly membership once again. Now know about the complainant BJP leader Akash Saxena After Azam Khan lost his Assembly membership, a by-election was held for the Rampur city seat on December 5, 2022. The results were declared on December 7. In the by-election, BJP candidate Akash Saxena defeated Azam Khan’s close aide Asim Raza by 25,703 votes. Earlier, Saxena had also contested against Azam Khan in the 2022 Assembly elections from Rampur but lost. Akash Saxena is directly involved as a complainant or party in 43 cases against Azam Khan. He is a businessman by profession and the son of former minister Shiv Bahadur Saxena.

stories.title: Power crisis in UP sparks political row:Minister AK Sharma hits back at Akhilesh as protests erupt over outrages
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh's power crisis has intensified amid the ongoing heatwave. Residents angry over prolonged power cuts staged protests in Lucknow, Varanasi and Kanpur on Friday. In Lucknow, people took to the streets at midnight and punctured the tyres of a junior engineer’s vehicle. In Varanasi, a youth frustrated by frequent outages reached a power station carrying his bedding and insisted on sleeping there. In Kanpur, Samajwadi Party leaders protested against power cuts, offered floral tributes to posters reading “Late Electricity System” and lit candles as a symbolic condolence. Meanwhile, Energy Minister AK Sharma has hit back at Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav. In a sarcastic remark, he said, “Akhilesh ji, whenever you pick up a mirror, look at yourself first and then show it to others.” Angered by Akhilesh’s statement, Sharma also posted a detailed 19-point response on X. In it, he referred to power supply and outages during previous SP governments. Akhilesh had posted on Friday that the BJP government, the power minister and corrupt contractors were responsible for the “major electricity disaster” in the state. He urged people not to vent their anger on junior employees or linemen of the power department. He said thousands of contractual employees had been removed from the department and the remaining staff were already working under immense pressure. According to him, the BJP government, power minister, MPs, MLAs, mayors, councillors, senior officials and corrupt contractors were all responsible for the ongoing crisis and should be held accountable. What did Minister AK Sharma say? In his post on X, AK Sharma said the SP chief appeared to view Uttar Pradesh’s power system as extremely weak. He wrote, “I would like to tell him—whenever you pick up a mirror, look at yourself first and then show it to others.” Referring to Akhilesh’s criticism, Sharma said, “As for the babool tree, the decision has already been made. You planted it and we are uprooting it completely.” He also attached another chart, claiming it showed the gap between power supply and consumption over the last 15 years. The picture is from Lucknow’s Ashiyana area, where Samajwadi Party leaders and workers staged a protest against power cuts. Read what Akhilesh said? In his post on X, Akhilesh wrote that people should not target power department employees or linemen for the unbearable electricity crisis caused by the BJP government’s wrong policies. He said that after the removal of thousands of contractual workers, the remaining staff were already under heavy pressure. He further alleged that the BJP government, power minister, BJP MPs, MLAs, mayors, councillors, senior officials and corrupt contractors were responsible for the “major electricity disaster” and should answer the public’s questions. Akhilesh claimed that the BJP government had paralysed the power sector. According to him, no new power plants had been set up to meet rising demand, nor had transmission or distribution systems been upgraded. He also alleged that the smart meter programme had become a major corruption issue, worsening the situation. Calling the situation condemnable, he said BJP leaders and their associates were threatening people who complained about power cuts. FIRs were allegedly being lodged against complainants, while even hospitals were struggling without reliable electricity. Mayawati also asked to find a solution for power cuts Earlier, BSP chief Mayawati also called on the government to address the power shortage. In a post on X, she wrote that inadequate power supply and outages during the intense summer had left people distressed in a large state like Uttar Pradesh. She said the poor, middle class, farmers, small traders and millions of hardworking people were suffering. She urged the government to take immediate measures and improve future power supply through the establishment of new power plants. The picture is from Lucknow, where residents angry over power cuts came out onto the streets on Friday night and blocked traffic at Budheshwar Crossing. Residents hit the streets in Lucknow over power cuts Power supply in Lucknow has come under severe strain amid the intense heatwave. Residents in several areas, frustrated by hours of outages, came out onto the streets at midnight. Electricity consumption in UP at record level amid severe heat Power demand in Uttar Pradesh has crossed 30,000 MW amid the ongoing heatwave. According to Vidyut Pravah, the portal that tracks electricity demand and consumption across the country, demand in Uttar Pradesh remained around 28,692 MW between 11.15 am and 11.30 am, almost equal to the 29,025 MW recorded during the same period a day earlier. The state government purchased nearly 577 MW of electricity from the power exchange market on the previous day at a cost of ₹2.20 per unit. Despite this, a shortage of around 850 MW, or 3.70%, was recorded during peak hours. The overall energy deficit stood at 9.80 million units, or around 2%. This indicates that electricity demand in the state remains extremely high. Even after purchasing additional power, shortages continue to be felt in some areas. Experts say that while the government is buying additional electricity, the infrastructure needed to deliver it to consumers remains inadequate. The state’s power transmission capacity—the ability to transport electricity over long distances from generation centres through high-voltage networks—is around 31,500 MW. Officials say that if the system operates at full capacity, several substations may trip. As a result, the state is unable to supply much beyond 31,000 MW despite demand being higher.

stories.title: Will Lucknow Mayor resign after High Court order:City’s top civic post loses powers for first time in UP
stories.summary: The Lucknow High Court has delivered a historic verdict. This is the first such case in which a court has stripped all powers of a mayor. The action was taken over the mayor’s failure to comply with an order issued six months ago regarding administering the oath to a Samajwadi Party councillor. The mayor is considered the most powerful person in a city. The protocol rank of the mayor is at the top. The mayor can issue important orders on special occasions and is responsible for maintaining basic civic facilities of the city. In Lucknow, the mayor’s financial and administrative powers will now remain frozen. The municipal commissioner and the district magistrate will oversee the functioning in her place. Experts believe that after the court order, the mayor should resign. However, it remains to be seen what stand the mayor will take next. What powers does a Mayor have? The mayor is considered the first citizen of the city and is the head of the municipal corporation. The mayor has control over their office and certain administrative functions. According to senior journalist Ratan Manilal, the mayor forms their own cabinet, known as the Mayor-in-Council (MIC). If the municipal corporation head is unable to function, the mayor can call special meetings. In situations like disasters or epidemics, the mayor also has the authority to take urgent decisions. In several cases, certain powers may also be delegated to the mayor by the Mayor-in-Council. How did the Mayor system start and how do cities function under it? The mayor is also called Mahapaur and is the head of the municipal corporation or municipality. Major cities in India have municipal corporations. These are cities with a population of 5 lakh or more and large geographical areas. Smaller towns are governed by municipal councils, whose heads are called municipal chairpersons. Is the Mayor just a ceremonial post? Experts say that to some extent, this can be considered true. The mayor is elected from among councillors and, in many cases, functions as a ceremonial position. The real executive, financial, and administrative powers of the city lie with the municipal commissioner, an IAS officer appointed by the government, who runs the entire municipal administration. Although the mayor is considered the first citizen of the city, the commissioner plays a more powerful role in key decisions and administration. Experts also note that mayors still do not have very strong powers or autonomy. They only have limited administrative and financial authority. Earlier, they were under state government control, which ended after the 1992 constitutional amendment. However, while their autonomy has increased, there have been continued demands to expand it further. How are Mayors elected in Uttar Pradesh? In some states, mayors are directly elected, while in others they are chosen by elected councillors or municipal members. However, in municipal corporations, the executive power remains with the municipal commissioner appointed by the government. This often leads to conflicts between the mayor and the commissioner. What do experts say about the Lucknow Mayor case? Senior journalist Ratan Manilal says that after a Samajwadi Party candidate won the election, failing to administer the oath amounts to not following the legal process, which is a serious lapse or contempt of court. Even though the mayor is an elected representative, she can be held responsible in this situation, and the court order can be seen as a form of punishment. This also raises questions about the validity of the mayor’s orders, as non-compliance with rules affects the legal standing of the office. According to Ratan Manilal, this entire issue should have been resolved earlier. The BJP candidate’s election had already been cancelled, and the person who needed to be sworn in was not administered the oath. This was an unnecessary conflict that could have been avoided from the beginning. What did the Lucknow mayor fail to comply with in the court order? Answer: Senior journalist Rajendra Kumar says the mayor violated court directions, which is why the court took this action. This decision is expected to directly impact the functioning of the municipal corporation. After the freezing of financial and administrative powers, several important decisions may now be put on hold. Following the High Court order, Sushma Kharkwal will not be able to take any decisions related to municipal administration. She may now have only the option of administering oath to ward councillor Lalit Kishore Tiwari. What powers will the Lucknow mayor not be able to exercise now? Experts say that once powers are frozen, development-related files will no longer be sent to the mayor. This will affect development work. Under Section 117 (Clause 5) of the Uttar Pradesh Municipal Act, 1959, the general execution of municipal functions is mentioned under the control of the mayor, but executive authority rests with the municipal commissioner. What is the full case? Answer: In the municipal election for Ward 73 of the Lucknow Municipal Corporation, BJP candidate Pradeep Shukla won. Samajwadi Party candidate Lalit Kishore Tiwari came second. Tiwari filed a petition in court alleging that Shukla had hidden information about a second marriage and other personal details in his nomination affidavit. The court cancelled Pradeep Shukla’s election and declared Lalit Kishore Tiwari the elected councillor for Ward 73 on 19 December 2025. However, the mayor did not administer the oath to Tiwari for five months. Tiwari then approached the court. On 21 May, the High Court held the mayor guilty of contempt and ordered the freezing of her administrative and financial powers. Meanwhile, the Mayor did not administer oath to Lalit Kishore for 5 months. On this, Tiwari went to court. On 21 May, the High Court considered it contempt of order by the Mayor and issued an order to seize his administrative and financial powers.

stories.title: Azam Khan, son Abdullah get 10-year jail term:Rampur court extends sentence by 3 years in fake PAN card case
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan and his son Abdullah Azam Khan will now serve 10 years in prison after a Rampur MP/MLA court enhanced their sentence in the fake PAN card case. On Saturday, the court increased their earlier seven-year jail term by three more years each while also imposing a fine of ₹5 lakh on both. The duo has been lodged in Rampur jail since November 17, 2025, when they were first convicted and fined ₹50,000 each in the same case. The sentence enhancement came after the Uttar Pradesh government appealed through ADGC Seema Rana on December 5, 2025, arguing that the offence was not merely a documentation irregularity but a serious case involving misuse of government identity documents and fraud. The prosecution had sought life imprisonment for both accused. The case dates back to the 2017 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections when Abdullah Azam contested from the Swar seat. According to investigators, he was ineligible to contest as he had not attained the minimum age of 25 years. His original date of birth was allegedly January 1, 1993, but a forged birth certificate obtained from the Lucknow Municipal Corporation reportedly showed his birth year as 1990. Based on the forged document, Abdullah allegedly secured fake PAN cards and later obtained two passports. The controversy surfaced after BSP candidate Nawab Kazim Ali Khan challenged Abdullah’s nomination, claiming he was underage during the election. Subsequent investigations found that forged age documents had been used, leading to the cancellation of Abdullah’s election and termination of his Assembly membership. In 2019, BJP leader Akash Saxena also filed a case alleging that Abdullah had fraudulently obtained two PAN cards in violation of rules. The case eventually led to legal action against Azam Khan, Abdullah Azam and Tanzeen Fatima. Despite this, Abdullah won the Swar Assembly seat again in 2022, but later lost his membership following another conviction carrying a sentence of over three years.

stories.title: ITBP personnel lay siege to Kanpur Commissionerate:Armed jawans storm police station over hospital row; cops retreat
stories.summary: In Kanpur, 40-50 armed ITBP personnel surrounded the Police Commissionerate. The personnel were angry over no action being taken on a colleague's complaint. ITBP personnel stood at various places throughout the premises. Seeing the personnel standing in force uniform and holding weapons in their hands, the policemen retreated. The atmosphere in the premises remained tense for about an hour. Later, lengthy discussions took place between the Police Commissioner, CMO and other officials, after which the matter was resolved. Actually, the mother of commando Vikas Singh, stationed at ITBP camp, Nirmala Devi, had undergone treatment for a stomach problem at Krishna Hospital located at Tatmill Chowraha. It is alleged that negligence occurred during treatment, due to which infection spread in her hand and later the hand had to be amputated. Angry over the incident, Vikas reached the Police Commissioner on Tuesday, May 19, carrying his mother's severed hand and demanded action against the hospital management. The Police Commissioner had handed over the matter to the CMO for investigation. The investigation committee formed by the CMO submitted a report, but no clear conclusion was reached and no action was taken. Angered by this, ITBP personnel reached the Police Commissioner's office with 50 jawans and officers. They demanded action. Considering the situation, the CMO was directed to conduct a re-investigation to clarify whether there was negligence on the hospital's part or not. CMO Haridatt Nemi stated- A team has been formed under the leadership of two senior officers to investigate the matter, which will visit the spot and conduct a thorough investigation of the entire case and submit its report. The officers included in the investigation team have also spoken with the representatives who came with ITBP. Some of their questions have been answered. See the pictures- Resident of Fatehpur, posted in Kanpur's Maharajpur Vikas Singh is originally a resident of Khaga Hathgaon in Fatehpur. Currently, Vikas is posted at the 32nd Battalion located in Maharajpur. The ITBP office is here. Vikas said that his 56-year-old mother Nirmala Devi had breathing problems. She was complaining of constipation and weakness. His mother was shown at the ITBP hospital located in Maharajpur. On May 13, 2026, his mother's health suddenly deteriorated, after which the doctors referred her to a higher center, i.e., a hospital included in ITBP's panel. Vikas took his mother in an ambulance. There was severe traffic jam on the way and his mother's condition was continuously deteriorating. Due to this, Vikas took her urgently to Krishna Hospital located in Tatmil. There, the doctors immediately put the mother on oxygen support and inserted a cannula (vigo) in her hand. Vikas alleges that the hospital doctors gave his mother the wrong injection. Due to this, her hand turned black. The swelling kept increasing continuously. When the mother's condition started worsening, she was admitted to Paras Hospital located at Bithoor Road Bakunthapur on the evening of May 14. On May 17, the doctors tried hard, but at this stage they were referred that infection had spread in the mother's hand. Because of this, the doctors had to amputate her hand. My mother's hand was cut off right in front of me Vikas Singh had said that I tried to find out from the doctors, but it could not be clarified why the infection occurred in the hand and why her hand had to be amputated. He alleged that this happened only due to the negligence of Krishna Hospital. Strict action should be taken against the hospital operator and doctors. These very hands of my mother raised me from childhood and made me this big. Today, my mother's hand was cut off right in front of me, even after being in the army I cannot get justice for my mother. Police Commissioner Raghuvir Lal took the entire matter seriously. He referred the matter to the CMO and asked to form a panel to investigate. Officer said- My constable and inspector have also died ITBP's Liaison Officer Arpit Singh had stated - I have also received information that a woman constable of ITBP has also died during treatment at Krishna Hospital. An inspector has also died due to negligence in treatment. Because of this, I myself have come here with my constable to file a complaint against this hospital. So that strict action can be taken against Krishna Hospital. In the matter, CMO Haridatt Nemi said that this SIT-level investigation is being conducted under the supervision of senior officers. The team is conducting a detailed investigation of the entire matter. It has also been clarified that the investigation will take time, as statements from all parties will have to be taken. Documents will have to be examined. Other necessary procedures will have to be completed.

stories.title: Cockroach Janata Party a foreign force, says BJP MLA:Nand Kishore Gurjar says, 'Hindu society has also gone astray'
stories.summary: BJP MLA Nand Kishore Gurjar has called the Cockroach Janta Party a foreign conspiracy. Gurjar said - An attempt is being made to spoil the country's atmosphere in the name of Cockroach Janta Party. Behind this is foreign funding and the hand of people connected to terrorism. Those with jihadist thinking from Pakistan, Bangladesh and Hindustan are following it. This conspiracy is being hatched with the help of opposition parties and foreign agencies. Some people from Hindu society have also been misled by them. Nandkishore Gurjar is a BJP MLA from Loni assembly constituency in Ghaziabad. He became an MLA for the first time in 2017. In 2022, he made the BJP lotus bloom for the second time. Read the key points of the BJP MLA... 1- Plan to create civil war-like situation MLA Nandkishor Gurjar said - I met a national general secretary of Congress in Delhi yesterday. He told me that a conspiracy has been hatched for three months to spoil the atmosphere in the country. A plan has been made to create civil war-like conditions. There is a plan to cause riots at various places. 2- Conspiracy being hatched to make castes fight among themselves Gurjar claimed that a conspiracy is being hatched to create tension and make different castes fight among themselves. They want to make Brahmins, Thakurs, Gurjars, and Kurmis fight with each other. This is part of the thinking of opposition parties and jihadis. Everyone has seen what happened earlier in the name of Emperor Mihir Bhoj. At that time, hawala funding was also detected. The Samajwadi Party wanted to incite riots then but was not successful. 3- Opposition parties are deliberately supporting the Cockroach Party He said - Opposition parties want to create instability in the country. Therefore, they now want to spoil the atmosphere by putting youth forward in the name of Cockroach Janata Party. Opposition parties are supporting this. They have been completely exposed now. Their conspiracy will not be allowed to succeed. Jihadist-minded cockroaches in Pakistan, Bangladesh and India are following the Cockroach Party. Due to which its number of followers is increasing rapidly. Some people from Hindu society are also associated with it. This is a conspiracy. stories.title: Heatwave in UP with 46.4°C temp:Zoo animals seek relief in water; power cuts trigger anger in Lucknow
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh is reeling under a severe heatwave, with temperatures crossing 45°C across several districts. Banda remained the hottest city on Friday, recording a maximum temperature of 46.4°C. On Saturday morning, Ghaziabad witnessed light rain and cloud cover, offering brief relief, while most other districts continued to face intense sunshine and hot winds. The Meteorological Department said a western disturbance active over central Assam may bring light clouds and drizzle in some areas bordering Delhi. A heatwave alert has been issued for 48 districts, with a red alert in Banda, Chitrakoot, Kaushambi, and Prayagraj. Night temperatures are also expected to remain high. Meanwhile, in Gorakhpur Zoo, a tigress was seen resting in a swimming pool, while in Etawah Safari Park, a lion and lioness were spotted playing in water, and a bear cooling off in a pond. In Lucknow, power cuts triggered protests overnight in several areas. In Rae Bareli, an FIR has been registered against 150 people who blocked a road, while in the Para area, residents allegedly punctured the tire of a JE’s vehicle after a 36-hour power outage. The state’s electricity demand has crossed 30,000 MW, with a shortage of around 850 MW (3.70%) reported the previous day. Heatwave impact on gadgets With temperatures crossing 45°C in many parts of the country, electronic devices like mobile phones, laptops, and power banks are heating up rapidly. This can lead to battery damage, reduced performance, and even sudden shutdowns. In today’s 'News you need,' we look at how extreme heat affects gadgets and the ways to protect them from overheating. See weather pictures- Lucknow's meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh said, Dry and hot winds coming from Balochistan and the Thar desert in Pakistan are directly reaching the plains of North India. This is why intense heat, typical of June, is being felt in May itself. On the other hand, a trough line is passing from Manipur, through northern UP. Due to this, easterly winds are blowing. This is making the heat feel 2C-3C higher than the actual temperature. Currently, there is no hope of relief from the heat and heatwave. How will the weather be for the next 5 days?

stories.title: Influencer student assaulted at Kashi Vidyapeeth after ‘fat’ remark:Claims she was chased and clothes were nearly torn
stories.summary: In Varanasi, a social media influencer was chased and beaten by two girls. The influencer, Vaishnavi, had come to Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapeeth to give an exam. After the exam ended, students were celebrating a farewell among themselves. During this time, around 4:30 PM, two girls surrounded Vaishnavi and pulled her hair, throwing her down and beating her. Vaishnavi said, "I was leaving after giving the paper. Then a girl said, 'Get her out of my sight.' I said, 'Shut up, fatty.' After that, she came running and started hitting me. Her friend was also with her, and she also hit me." Many girls tried to intervene, but the two did not let go of me. They kept hitting me continuously. During this, the college guards standing there also did not try to save me. They also remained silent spectators. See 2 pictures Full case details Vaishnavi is a Mass Communication student at Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith. She is also an Instagram influencer. She has been a topper for two semesters. On Friday morning, from 9 AM to 12 PM, she had her last fourth-semester exam in the Faculty of Humanities. After the exams were over, the students stayed back in college and enjoyed themselves. Everyone was writing messages on each other's T-shirts, cherishing memories. Just then, Vaishnavi's classmates Priya and Aishwarya suddenly grabbed her and started beating her. Hearing the noise, many students gathered at the spot. Some female students tried to intervene and separate the three. But both girls continued to hit Vaishnavi. They pushed her to the ground. Vaishnavi called them fat, and the girls started beating her Student Vaishnavi said she had gone to appear for an exam at Kashi Vidyapeeth when the incident took place. She claimed that as she was leaving after the exam, a girl allegedly said, ‘She is going in front of me, get her out of my way.’ In response, she told her to ‘shut up, fatty.’ Vaishnavi said the girl then started shouting, but she ignored it and moved ahead. However, the girl, along with Prachi Pandey and Aishwarya Pandey, allegedly chased her inside the campus, assaulted her, and threw her to the ground. Alleged assault on campus In a conversation with Dainik Bhaskar, Vaishnavi said while crying that she feels the incident was a conspiracy to defame her. She alleged, ‘They tried to tear my clothes. I understand this now,’ before breaking down. Students of Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith said there had been an ongoing dispute between Vaishnavi and the other girls. On Friday, the argument escalated, and both sides exchanged abuses. Vaishnavi further said that after finding her alone, the two girls allegedly assaulted her. She also claimed that a young man’s name has surfaced in the matter, though his identity has not yet been confirmed. 2 accounts on Instagram, thousands of followers Vaishnavi has two accounts on Instagram. The first account is named queen_of_hell18, which has 82 thousand followers. The second account is named vaishnavii_official. This also has about 90 thousand followers. Vaishnavi makes reels related to beauty products, lifestyle, and daily essentials. Inspector Sigra Shivkant Mishra said- The matter is in cognizance, but no complaint has been filed by any party yet. Information about the entire matter is being gathered by talking to the Chief Proctor.

stories.title: Power cut leads to tragedy in Barabanki:4 dead, 1 critical as dumper runs over family sleeping outside
stories.summary: A tragic road accident in Barabanki claimed the lives of four members of a family after an out-of-control dumper truck ran over them late Friday night. The incident took place around 2 am in the Fatehpur police station area. According to reports, the family was sleeping outside their house due to a power outage when the speeding dumper first hit a tree and then ran over them. Locals rushed to the spot after hearing screams and shifted the injured to the district hospital, where doctors declared four of them dead. The deceased have been identified as Neeraj (35), his son Anurag (13), and two daughters Anshika (10) and Anshu (6). Neeraj’s wife Aarti (35) is critically injured and has been referred to Lohia Hospital in Lucknow. After the accident, the driver fled the scene, abandoning the dumper. Neeraj, a resident of Jhansa village, used to support his family by driving a rented Magic van. See pictures Neeraj's maternal uncle, Kripa Ram, said, Around three in the morning, a call came that an accident had happened. After that, we reached the hospital. Due to a power outage, everyone, troubled by the heat, was sleeping at the door in front of the house, when a dumper ran over them. Sister cried and said that everything is over Neeraj's sister Kiran is in a terrible state, crying inconsolably. She collapsed after seeing the children's bodies in the hospital. She cried and said, everything is over. Brother and the children are dead. When sister-in-law was taken from here to Lucknow, she was also unconscious. Brother and sister-in-law got married 14 years ago. The whole family lived happily together. Now nothing is left. The district hospital doctor said, All the injured were brought to the hospital around 5:15 AM. Among them, two children had died before reaching the hospital. One woman was referred to Lucknow after primary treatment.

stories.title: 7 arrested for cheating in SSC online exam:Centre set up in Greater Noida, used proxy server to solve papers
stories.summary: UP STF has busted a gang involved in rigging Staff Selection Commission (SSC) online examinations. The Noida STF unit raided Balaji Digital Zone examination centre in Knowledge Park on Friday night. Seven accused, including the alleged mastermind, were arrested from the spot. One candidate was also among those held. According to STF, the gang was cheating in the CAPF, SSF Constable (GD), and Assam Rifles Rifleman recruitment exam 2026 using a proxy server. Officials said the group did not hack the exam system but bypassed the company server by installing a proxy server, allowing outside solvers to solve papers through screen-sharing applications. Investigations revealed that the main accused, Pradeep Chauhan, had been running the racket for a long time and had set up the Balaji Digital Zone exam centre. Police recovered ₹50 lakh cash, laptops, mobile phones, routers, and a list of candidates. All accused are residents of Uttar Pradesh. Center operator turned out to be the mastermind Paper set cost 4 lakhs The investigation revealed that the gang used to extort up to ₹4 lakh from a candidate. In return, they guaranteed passing the exam. Out of this, ₹50 thousand were given to the agent who brought the candidate, while the remaining amount was distributed among Pradeep Chauhan, Amit Rana, and the solver. The job of the accused named Sandeep Bhati was to find candidates who wanted to pass the exam by paying money. He has worked as a lab supervisor in various companies. One candidate also caught Police have also arrested candidate Vivek Kumar in this case. He had arrived to take the exam and was preparing to get the paper solved through the gang. Those arrested Know how does a proxy server works? An STF official said that nowadays many exams are conducted online, where students take exams from laptops or computers. Here, some people resort to proxy servers or proxy software to pass the exam incorrectly. In this method, the student sets up a proxy software or tool (such as UltraViewer, AnyDesk, or special proxy tools) on their computer. The student merely pretends to sit in front of the computer, while another person (solver/hacker) sitting far away from the examination centre completely controls the student's screen via a proxy connection and ticks all the answers themselves. Proxy tools work in such a way that the examination software believes everything is normal, and it cannot easily detect this deception running in the background. These people create a main server where they download the paper. How is it done? An STF officer explained According to IT experts, a proxy server acts as an intermediate system that connects examination centre computers to the main SSC server. SSC sends question papers from its main server to different centres, where each centre downloads the paper to its local server at a scheduled time via the internet. All computers in the lab are then connected to the centre’s server through switches and Cat-6 cables. The alleged tampering happens here, where those involved in cheating connect a separate Cat-6 line and use remote access software like AnyDesk to gain system access. A link is then created using the candidate’s name and seat number. Once opened, the exam paper is accessed on their system, after which outside solvers solve the paper and send back answers, enabling the cheating network. SSC GD being held in 4 phases The SSC GD examination is being conducted in 4 phases from April 27 to May 30.

stories.title: ‘Brother killed by crocodile to avenge love marriage’:Man in Gonda alleges in-laws plotted brother’s murder
stories.summary: A young man in Gonda was reportedly dragged away by a crocodile while he was preparing his mother-in-law’s pyre on Wednesday. His body was recovered from the Saryu River 24 hours later. The deceased’s brother has alleged a conspiracy, claiming the incident was linked to family revenge over a love marriage. The post-mortem was conducted after 2 pm on Friday. Dr Aditya Gaur stated that the death occurred due to severe injuries, adding that 5–6 tooth marks were found on the neck and abdomen. He also noted that the crocodile attempted to bite the right hand but could not fully chew it. The victim, Deepak, was cremated at 6 pm in Ayodhya by his elder brother Sanjay Kumar. Meanwhile, a disaster expert in Gonda said the crocodile involved was small, which is why it could not consume the body. Bhaskar's team visited Deeha village, about 35 km from the district headquarters, where they spoke with the grieving family and reported their account of the incident. Read the ground report Deepak arrived at his in-laws' house for his mother-in-law's demise Deepak Verma (30), a resident of Pari Chowk Sigma 2 in Noida, had come to Gonda after the death of his mother-in-law. 6 years ago, Deepak had a love marriage with Rekha, a resident of Deeha village. Deepak worked in a private company in Noida. Deepak and Rekha have a 4-year-old daughter named Nikki. Rekha's father, Lalchand Sharma, has already passed away. Her mother, Urmila (50), had died on Tuesday due to cancer. Rekha has two other sisters and a younger brother named Raj. On Wednesday, preparations for the last rites were underway on the banks of the Saryu river near Sanauli Mohammadpur Udaybhan Pahi. Crocodile attack during funeral ritual Around 12 pm, Deepak and others reached the riverbank for the funeral rites. While he was hammering a stake into the ground to prepare the pyre, he later went to the river to wash his hands. At that moment, a crocodile suddenly emerged and grabbed his head. Despite people rushing and shouting to save him, the crocodile dragged Deepak into the water. Read the brother's allegations Family had arranged the marriage in the temple Deepak's younger brother, Badal, with a choked voice, said that we are 5 brothers. Deepak bhaiya was the second one. Father Ram Prakash had passed away some time ago. Bhaiya had informed about his affair with Bhabhi 6 years ago. After this, both were married in a temple. On Thursday, we booked two cars from Noida and reached Gonda. Until 3 PM, family members kept waiting outside the post-mortem house in the scorching heat. If Bhaiya's body had been received on time, the last rites would not have been delayed. Deepak started living separately Badal said that for one and a half years after the marriage, all of us, mother, brother-sister-in-law lived together. After that, some differences arose, and Deepak took a rented house 3 km away from home. He started living there with his wife. After some time, their daughter was born. After marriage, the brother had come to Gonda only once. Accusing of conspiracy, the brother said, How would someone who doesn't live here know? The local residents knew that crocodiles live in that area. Still, they sent my brother there. If someone has come to attend a funeral, would you make them work? Why was he allowed to go to such a dangerous area? Deepak's brother Badal said, I myself went near the river and saw the spot where my brother was dragged by a crocodile. That is a very dangerous area. People present nearby said that 20-25 crocodiles live here. Deepak brother had come here alone. I think all this was deliberately done by him as part of a conspiracy. His death should be investigated. Mother's pain My daughter-in-law has lost everything Deepak’s mother, Vimla Devi, said she met her daughter-in-law Rekha, who is in a deep shock and keeps crying, screaming, and fainting. She said the family has “lost everything” and alleged that no help has been provided even after 24 hours, demanding government compensation. She called the incident ‘murder’ and questioned the presence of crocodiles in the area, saying outsiders would not know the danger. She also recalled that Deepak had informed the family about his wife, after which they got them married in a temple. She said he had recently met her while coming to Gonda and informed her about his mother-in-law’s death. She added that she gave him money she had and the family hired two vehicles for ₹30,000 to travel to Gonda. Child has become an orphan Mother-in-law Vimla Devi said that she doesn't know what her daughter-in-law will do in the future. The poor child has become an orphan. Who will raise her? Therefore, the only demand from the government is that the aid money should be given in the name of my granddaughter. Badal's paternal grandfather-in-law, Babulal, also said that the compensation amount should be given in the name of Deepak's daughter, so that she can be raised. Meanwhile, Umri Begumganj Station House Officer Chandan Kumar said - According to doctors, Deepak's body was somewhat decomposed. Therefore, without delay, the body was handed over to the family. After the last rites in Ayodhya, the victim's family has said that they will perform the remaining rituals from Greater Noida. Officials said that small crocodile could not eat a man District Disaster Specialist Rajesh Kumar Srivastava had informed about the recovery of the body around 12 noon on Thursday. He had said that the crocodile had tried to eat some part of the right hand of the body by biting it. It had also tried to bite the shoulder, but could not eat that either. Bite marks were also found near Deepak's right ear. Possibly, the crocodile was small, which is why it couldn't make the youth its prey. However, it has been confirmed that the crocodile dragged the youth away. People who were with Deepak saw him being dragged into the river.
