stories.title: Brijesh Singh set to launch son in Dhananjay’s stronghold:Two leaders planning strategy behind the scenes; MLC becomes active in Jaunpur
stories.summary: More than eight months remain before the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, but a fresh political battle appears to be taking shape in Purvanchal. Discussions have intensified over the possible entry of former MLC Brijesh Singh into Jaunpur, considered the political stronghold of strongman leader Dhananjay Singh. Brijesh Singh is reportedly planning to field his son Siddharth Singh in the district panchayat elections. Sources claim he wants to establish political control in Jaunpur through this move. According to political insiders, BJP leader Kripashankar Singh and Apna Dal’s former MP Kunwar Harivansh Singh are playing key roles in the strategy. Harivansh Singh’s relations with Dhananjay Singh have reportedly remained strained for years, while Kripashankar Singh is also considered politically opposed to him. Read the special report Brijesh Singh becomes active in Jaunpur Jaunpur has long been regarded as Dhananjay Singh’s political bastion. His influence extends from the Malhani Assembly constituency to the district panchayat structure. His wife, Srikala Reddy, currently serves as the District Panchayat President. Now, Brijesh Singh and Siddharth Singh have also begun actively engaging in local politics. On May 9, Brijesh Singh arrived in Jaunpur with his son and attended a Maharana Pratap Jayanti programme in Badlapur. BJP MLA Rameshchandra Mishra, former MP Harivansh Singh and several other leaders welcomed them at the event. Political circles are discussing the possibility of Siddharth Singh contesting the Zila Panchayat election either from Jaunpur’s Kerakat block seat or from Bhadohi. Siddharth had also prepared to contest the Bhadohi Zila Panchayat elections in 2021, but eventually stayed out of the race. What does Dhananjay Singh say about Brijesh Singh’s entry? In a recent podcast interview, Dhananjay Singh was asked about Brijesh Singh entering politics in Jaunpur. Responding without hesitation, he said- Who is Brijesh Singh? This is a democracy where everyone has the right to do politics and serve the public. It is not as if only we can do politics. Whoever wants to enter the field is welcome. People should contest elections and work for society. When I am not afraid of major political parties, there is no question of fearing one individual. Dhananjay’s rivals working behind the scenes Sources claim Kripashankar Singh and former MP Harivansh Singh are playing crucial roles in the emerging political strategy against Dhananjay Singh. Kripashankar Singh previously served as Minister of State for Home Affairs and MLA in the Congress government in Maharashtra. He contested the 2024 Lok Sabha elections from Jaunpur on a BJP ticket but lost. His supporters allege that Dhananjay Singh’s influence contributed to that defeat. Meanwhile, tensions between Dhananjay Singh and Harivansh Singh reportedly date back to 2017. At the time, a no-confidence motion was moved against Khuthan Block Pramukh Sarju Devi Yadav, who was considered close to SP leader and former minister Lalai Yadav. Harivansh Singh was said to be backing the move because he wanted his daughter-in-law, Neelam Singh, to become Block Pramukh. On the other side, Lalai Yadav and Dhananjay Singh joined forces to stop the no-confidence motion. The political clash allegedly escalated into indiscriminate firing between supporters of both camps. Harivansh Singh later filed an attempt-to-murder case against Dhananjay Singh. However, in 2023, following a mutual settlement, he withdrew his statement in court and Dhananjay was acquitted. Political observers now believe Brijesh Singh’s entry is part of a broader attempt to challenge Dhananjay Singh’s hold over Jaunpur. Challenging Dhananjay Singh will not be easy Jaunpur’s politics has historically revolved around land dominance, contracting networks and muscle power. Since the 1990s, Thakur leaders have reportedly maintained influence over public works contracts, railway projects, mining operations and local business syndicates in the district. Their economic strength has also translated into electoral influence and campaign management. Among them, Dhananjay Singh remains the most dominant political figure. The Rari Assembly seat, now known as Malhani, has long been regarded as his political fortress. Over the years, Dhananjay Singh expanded beyond traditional caste politics and cultivated a “Robin Hood” image that helped him gain support among Brahmins, Yadavs and Dalits as well. Whether Dhananjay Singh is in jail, contesting as an Independent candidate, or whether his wife Srikala Reddy is contesting elections, political observers say the district closely watches every move made by the family. In such circumstances, if Brijesh Singh fields his son in Jaunpur, the contest may evolve beyond electoral politics into a prestige battle between two influential strongman families. Both camps seen as close to BJP Interestingly, both factions are viewed as politically close to the BJP. Brijesh Singh’s family has long been regarded as supportive of the party. Meanwhile, Dhananjay Singh has recently been increasing his proximity to BJP leader Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh. The two leaders have been seen together at several events in recent weeks. On May 11, Srikala Reddy also met Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. Against this backdrop, political activity in Jaunpur is expected to become even more intense in the coming months ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections.

stories.title: 'CJI should not have said it', Iqra on ‘Cockroach Party’:Says being called ‘Mulli’ taught her to develop a thick skin in politics
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party MP Iqra Hasan has been in the spotlight after clashing with the police during a protest in Saharanpur over the alleged murder of a youth. An FIR was later registered against her, but she says she will not back down. Speaking to Dainik Bhaskar, Iqra spoke openly about the Saharanpur protest, the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, women’s reservation, social media trolling and her political journey. She also responded sharply to Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath’s remarks on offering namaz on roads, saying, “Who is he trying to scare?” Below are edited excerpts from the conversation- The Chief Minister made a statement on offering namaz on roads. How do you see it? Now no one offers namaz on the roads. Perhaps he has been misinformed. People only offer prayers on roads during Eid because mosques do not have enough space. Who he is trying to scare is beyond comprehension. Namaz lasts only five to ten minutes. No one wants to pray on the roads. The Kanwar Yatra is about to begin and it passes through my area. We welcome it. This is the beauty of our country. If we remove these traditions, who will preserve them? In 2022, RLD was with SP, but not anymore. How will that affect 2027? The 2024 election was a huge challenge for us. The way our national president Akhilesh Yadav gave the PDA slogan united people. Because of that, SP’s vote share and seat tally increased. Similarly, in the 2027 elections, we will defeat the BJP and form the government. Akhilesh Yadav keeps questioning the Election Commission. What reforms are needed? There is a lot of scope for improvement, but we have no hope from the Election Commission at all. The way elections in Bengal and Bihar were allegedly hijacked in favour of the BJP, it appears the Commission is working for them. We are strengthening our booth-level system ourselves and closely monitoring voting patterns and turnout. SP supported Mamata Banerjee in Bengal, but she lost. Has that reduced confidence? No. Every state has different equations and political thinking. The people of Uttar Pradesh are politically aware. UP has always shaped the direction of national politics. We are hopeful that people in UP will bring change in 2027 and form an SP government. The amendment to the Women’s Reservation Bill was defeated in the Lok Sabha. BJP is now making it an issue? You are right. The amendment was defeated and the reservation bill remains unchanged. BJP has no intention of implementing the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam passed in 2023. Otherwise, they would have notified the law by now. Our demand is clear, women should get 33% reservation across all 543 Lok Sabha seats. This is propaganda meant to mislead women. What do you think about people using words like ‘Mulli’? Unfortunately, some people use such words without understanding others’ feelings. In politics, one’s skin becomes thick over time, but I am still new and learning. I focus on those who support me. Out of nearly 10 lakh votes, I received 5.25 lakh, while around 4 lakh went to the opposition. Naturally, some people will oppose me. Prime Minister Narendra Modi recently posed with Giorgia Meloni and gifted her Melody chocolates. What is your view? He asked people not to buy gold, not to travel abroad and not to drive cars to save fuel. But then such photographs emerge. It feels like a slap in the face for ordinary people — as if rulers can do anything while the public must remain submissive. ‘The administration behaved dictatorially’ Why did you sit on a protest in Saharanpur? An elderly woman’s son had been murdered. I went to meet the DIG, but the family’s pleas were ignored. Some of the family members accompanying them were jailed after what we believe were baseless allegations. In such a situation, it was our duty to help them. What happened reflected dictatorship, and our protest was against that. The electricity was cut at the police station. How did the protest end? Initially, I was taken to another police station. Later, we learnt that members of the victim’s family had been sent to jail. Barricades were erected and we were not allowed to re-enter the district. When we sat inside the police station, the electricity supply was cut. As crowds began gathering, the administration approved the family members’ bail that very night. After that, the protest ended. Was this a breach of privilege? Will you raise it in Parliament? We are opposition MPs. Breaches of privilege happen all the time with us. Protocols are ignored. Only we know how we are spoken to behind closed doors. Even ruling party leaders are often not heard. The difference is that they cannot speak openly. We stand firm. Forget protocol — at least show some humanity. ‘My father remains my inspiration’ Your personality and Dimple Yadav’s are both considered simple and grounded. What do you think? I do not think comparisons are appropriate. Dimple Yadav has her own stature. Her nature is very good and the way she leads the party inspires us all. My political journey has only just begun. Who is your role model in politics or personal life? My father. I am in politics because of him. You grew up in a political family. Does that create pressure? Of course. You are compared with big personalities and expectations are equally high. I cannot completely replicate my father’s political style, but people expect similar things from me. So yes, there is pressure, but it also feels good when people remember my father through me. People often ask when you are getting married? Not yet. Whenever it happens, it will not be kept secret. What do you do in your free time? Nothing much. I either watch television or stay at home. If my phone does not ring for a day, that feels peaceful. ‘Smart meters are a major issue in Kairana’ What is the biggest problem in Kairana right now? Smart electricity meters are currently a major issue. People are facing problems with electricity connections and inflated bills after smart meters were installed. Weavers are also struggling and the quality of education is declining. Work is being done on these issues. Does polarisation politics still dominate western UP? No. I think the farmers’ movement changed the atmosphere in the region. I am a living example of that. In my constituency, where around 30% of the population is Muslim, people from all communities voted for me and sent me to Parliament. How satisfied are you with spending MP funds? The MP fund is not enough. Either it should be abolished or increased to match MLA funds. We try to ensure development work reaches every community and village where it is needed most. I also want to establish a degree college in my area and have discussed it with Minority Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju. ‘The CJI’s remark was not right’ The CJI remarked the “Cockroach Janata Party”. What is your reaction? I think such comments can be seen as rebellious humour, but it is not right to belittle people. Everyone wants to express their views for the betterment of the country. In my opinion, the CJI’s comment was inappropriate. As for the “Cockroach Samaj Party”, people are now joining it through memes. If the “Cockroach Janata Party” comes to power in UP, what will happen? In 2027, the Samajwadi Party is coming to power. We will think about the rest later. What should SP do to increase women’s participation in politics? It has to begin at the booth level. Women leaders need to be prepared from the grassroots. Whenever the women’s reservation bill is eventually implemented, every party will need strong women leaders. More young women should join politics. Also, the practice of ‘Pradhanpati’ in villages should not enter Parliament. What is the solution to sugarcane farmers’ problems in western UP? The government needs to increase sugarcane prices. The current rates are not sufficient and farmers in UP get lower prices compared to neighbouring states. Our national president has promised that if an SP government is formed, farmers will receive payments digitally within 24 hours. I myself have joined protests alongside farmers several times. How do you deal with trolling on social media? Social media trolling is like a swamp, the deeper you go into it, the more you sink. One should not pay too much attention to it. Perhaps some people earn their livelihood through trolling. Know about the incident where Iqra had to protest in Saharanpur

His parents have also voiced concerns about his safety and potential arrest due to the party's rapid online popularity.

stories.title: A 13-year-old built a LEGO Braille printer to make reading more affordable
stories.summary: A 13-year-old American innovator, Shubham Banerjee, revolutionized Braille printing with Braigo, a remarkably affordable device built from Lego blocks. This invention addresses the high cost of traditional embossers, making tactile reading accessible to more visually impaired individuals. Braigo's simple design and focus on affordability have garnered significant attention, highlighting the power of user-centric problem-solving.

5K women 50+ category: age, experience, and the spirit to keep moving | Times Internet Half Marathon 2026
In 2017, Colorado construction workers accidentally dug up a very rare dinosaur fossil
stories.summary: A construction project in Thornton, Colorado, unearthed a significant prehistoric find. Workers discovered a fossilised skeleton initially thought to be a Triceratops. Further examination revealed it was a much rarer Torosaurus. This discovery, comprising 80 per cent of the skull and 15 per cent of the body, is one of the most complete Torosaurus specimens found in Colorado.

stories.title: As West Asia burns, four-decades-old war wounds reopen in an Indian family
‘Afraid for my life’: Jhalmuri vendor who served PM Modi facing death threats from Pakistan, Bangladesh
stories.summary: A jhalmuri vendor from Jhargram, who served Prime Minister Modi, claims to be receiving threatening calls from Pakistan and Bangladesh. The vendor, Vikram Sao, has informed the police, who have provided security. Sao, the sole breadwinner, fears for his safety while cycling and has appealed to the PM for protection after his interaction went viral.

stories.title: PM Modi, Cyprus President Christodoulides hold talks to deepen bilateral ties
How streetlights may be affecting birds, bats and insects at night in ways scientists did not expect
‘Unable to save them’: Two Indian mountaineers die during Everest descent
stories.summary: Mount Everest, often a site of triumph, turned somber as two Indian climbers, Arun Kumar Tiwari and Sandeep Are, tragically lost their lives while descending from its peak. Reports confirmed their deaths on Friday, with experts suggesting extreme fatigue was to blame.

stories.title: In 2000, an amateur explorer found a hidden cave in France filled with ancient art and burials
stories.summary: A hidden cave in France's Dordogne region, Cussac Cave, revealed thousands of years of history when explorer Marc Delluc discovered detailed Upper Palaeolithic art. Further exploration uncovered an intact human skeleton, suggesting the cave served as a prehistoric burial site and a place of worship. Remarkably, ancient footprints preserved in the mud indicate the use of sophisticated footwear.

stories.title: 'Content, not individuals': Supreme Court tones down remarks against academicians in NCERT row
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has assured three academics that harsh remarks against them in a previous order will be deleted. These remarks stemmed from a Class 8 NCERT chapter on judicial corruption. The court clarified its concern was the chapter's content, not the individuals, emphasizing the need for balanced academic discussions on the judiciary while respecting constitutional frameworks.

stories.title: ‘It’s not their fault’: Amazon UK boss says education system is failing young workers
In 2002, cavers found a hidden skeleton that revealed an ancient Australian predator
stories.summary: Explorers found an ancient marsupial lion skeleton in a Nullarbor Plain cave. This discovery offers a unique look at extinct life. The cave's stable environment preserved the fossil for millions of years. Researchers are studying the skeleton to understand the predator's strength and hunting abilities. This find reveals a hidden world beneath the desert surface.

stories.title: Rajya Sabha Polls 2026: Election commission announces date for Upper House elections
stories.summary: Polling for the Rajya Sabha elections will take between 9 am and 4 pm, with counting scheduled to begin at 5 pm the same day. The Election Commission said the entire poll process will conclude by June 20. The Commission clarified that voters will be allowed to use only the integrated violet sketch pens supplied by the Returning Officer for marking preferences on ballot papers. Use of any other pen during voting will not be permitted.

stories.title: Britain rolls out landmark transgender rules for single sex toilets, NHS wards and women-only spaces
stories.summary: Britain's new transgender access rules, following a Supreme Court ruling, allow single-sex spaces to exclude trans individuals if proportionate for privacy, safety, or dignity. This impacts healthcare, sports, and workplaces, sparking national debate on inclusion and rights. Organizations must balance protections, with case-by-case assessments encouraged.

stories.title: New anti-Hindu hate monitor launched in UK amid rise in religious hate crimes
43-foot ‘marine T rex’ bigger than great white sharks and more brutal than any mosasaur discovered in Texas
'Muttatthengu' in Tamil Nadu: DMK takes 'bent coconut tree' jibe at VCK over CM Vijay's cabinet
stories.summary: A literary spat erupts in Tamil Nadu politics as DMK leader A Raja's 'coconut tree' metaphor targets VCK and IUML joining CM Vijay's new government. VCK and the ruling TVK hit back, accusing the DMK of arrogance and questioning their own past alliances and commitment to social justice.

stories.title: 'People calling to offer condolences': Twisha Sharma's mother-in-law Giribala Singh denies speaking to influencial people
stories.summary: Retired judge Giribala Singh denies allegations of contacting influential figures after her daughter-in-law Twisha Sharma's death. She claims calls were for condolences and accuses local police of pressure. Sharma's family alleges dowry harassment and abetment to suicide. The husband, Samarth Singh, remains absconding. The case involves FIRs under the Bharatiya Nyay Sanhita and Dowry Prohibition Act.

'We do not want him in politics': Parents of Cockroach Janata Party founder Abhijeet Dipke fear arrest
stories.summary: Parents of 'Cockroach Janta Party' founder Abhijeet Dipke express deep anxiety over his viral political satire platform, fearing legal trouble and arrest. Dipke, a Boston University student, launched the campaign a week ago, amassing millions of followers. His parents urge him to abandon politics for a safer career, citing his own expressed fears of detention upon returning to India.

stories.title: 'Where is her husband?': Twisha Sharma's brother questions whereabouts after Samarth Singh missing for 10 days
stories.summary: Twisha Sharma's family questions husband Samarth Singh's anticipatory bail plea amid dowry harassment and suicide allegations. They accuse his mother, a retired judge, of intimidation and question the delay in FIR registration. Police have issued a Look Out Circular for Samarth, who claims the prosecution's case is based on 'imagination'.

stories.title: 'Quran mandates qurbani': AJUP chief Humayun Kabir stirs row after Bengal cattle slaughter curb
stories.summary: A political storm erupted in West Bengal as AJUP chief Humayun Kabir vowed to conduct cow slaughter for Eid, defying state restrictions. He insisted the Quran mandates it, challenging the government's notice. BJP countered, emphasizing law enforcement and opposing illegal slaughter, while some Muslim leaders urged respect for cows.

Most advanced countries in the world ranked: From South Korea’s high digital adoption to Denmark’s pharmaceutical innovation

stories.summary: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister M.K. Stalin expanded his cabinet, inducting Vanni Arasu from VCK and AM Shahjahan from IUML. This move strengthens coalition representation, bringing the total number of ministers to 33. The expansion follows a recent reshuffle, with key portfolios like Finance and Revenue reassigned.

stories.summary: The Competition Commission of India raised alarms about the practices of private super-specialty hospitals in the Delhi NCR region. It was highlighted that patients find themselves in a 'locked-in' predicament, where they're almost forced to rely on the hospitals' own pharmacies and diagnostic services.

stories.title: NEET row: NTA tells parliamentary panel leak did not happen from its system
stories.summary: A parliamentary committee questioned the NTA chief regarding the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak, with the director stating the leak did not originate from their system. The committee also reviewed NTA reforms and discussed the impact of AI on education, alongside challenges faced by Aligarh Muslim University and the National Commission for Minority Educational Institutions.

stories.title: 'If I do attend, I get killed': Donald Trump says he 'has a thing called Iran' stopping him from attending son's wedding
stories.summary: Amid escalating Iran tensions, President Trump expressed uncertainty about attending his son Donald Trump Jr.'s wedding this weekend in the Bahamas. He joked about facing criticism from the "fake news" regardless of his attendance, citing security concerns and the difficult timing due to international developments.

Govt weighing steps to check current account deficit: Piyush Goyal

stories.summary: Asmongold responded harshly after Nina Lin blamed him and his viewers for a situation that allegedly led to her spending a night in jail over unscanned $4 scissors. During a livestream, Nina suggested an Asmongold viewer reported her to police. Asmongold mocked her claims, called the incident “stupid,” and predicted she would “end up in jail again,” escalating the viral feud across Twitch and social media platforms.

The No Jumper podcaster and rapper became known through YouTube videos, music, and podcast appearances. Following the arrest news, No Jumper hosts reacted during a livestream and expressed shock while speaking about his recent online success and growing platform.

Despite the frightening arrival of numerous police officers, she maintained a positive attitude, even finding the experience "kinda fun." The incident drew widespread anger online, with many supporting her efforts and hoping for increased donations.

stories.summary: Air France and Airbus have been found guilty of manslaughter by a Paris appeals court for the 2009 crash of Flight 447, which killed all 228 people on board. The court overturned a previous ruling, holding both companies responsible for the tragedy. Fined €225,000 each, the companies plan to appeal the verdict, while victims' families seek greater accountability.

stories.summary: India's space regulator is offering full technology transfer for the reliable PSLV rocket to private firms, aiming to boost commercial launches. This follows a similar move for the SSLV. Despite delays in the first industry-built PSLV and SSLV, the government seeks an industry-driven launch ecosystem, signaling a major shift from ISRO's production model.

stories.summary: India's power demand hit an unprecedented 270.8 GW due to intense heat and widespread air conditioner use, nearing 2026 projections. This marks the fourth consecutive day of record-breaking demand. Officials assure grid stability, attributing local outages to distribution issues. Further demand hikes are anticipated as extreme temperatures persist.

stories.summary: NTA chief Abhishek Singh told a parliamentary panel the NEET-UG 2026 paper wasn't leaked via their system, with the CBI investigating. Officials presented reforms, noting 70% of Radhakrishnan Committee recommendations are implemented. The agency faces a 25% staff shortage and is considering computer-based testing for future exams.

stories.title: Boo of Jobs: Real anger about Artificial Intelligence at US convocations
stories.summary: Graduates across America are booing speakers who mention artificial intelligence. This reaction stems from worries about automation impacting jobs and the perception that AI benefits the wealthy. Communities are also protesting data centers due to environmental concerns. The backlash highlights a growing public skepticism about technological progress outpacing democratic consent.

'Forced to convert and marry': 23-year-old woman accuses man she met online abuse over years
stories.summary: A 23-year-old woman has accused a man and his associates of kidnapping, gang-raping, and forcing her into marriage after allegedly coercing religious conversion in Jamia Nagar. Police have arrested four of the six accused, with the main suspect already in jail for another case. The woman reported being befriended online and sexually assaulted repeatedly between 2021 and 2025.

stories.title: Punjab health scheme provides Rs 522 crore in cashless treatment
Not an essential part of Eid: Calcutta HC refuses to stay cattle slaughter restrictions ahead of festival
stories.summary: The Calcutta High Court has upheld the West Bengal government's restrictions on slaughtering certain animals ahead of Bakr Eid. The court found the notification aligned with previous directives, emphasizing that cow sacrifice isn't a mandatory Islamic practice. Authorities must now decide on exemptions within 24 hours, ensuring proper certification and infrastructure for any permitted slaughter.

stories.title: Umar Khalid moves Delhi HC seeking 15-day interim bail after trial court rejected 'unreasonable' plea
stories.summary: Umar Khalid has approached the Delhi High Court for 15 days' interim bail, from May 22 to June 5, to attend his uncle's Chehlum ceremony and care for his mother undergoing surgery. A trial court had previously denied his request, deeming it not necessary. Khalid argues the trial court's assessment was incorrect.

stories.title: Bosch bets on JVs to speed up next-gen mobility push
stories.summary: German auto technology supplier Bosch is shifting towards partnerships and joint ventures to accelerate development and market entry in new mobility technologies. This strategic move, exemplified by a new JV with TSF Group for commercial vehicle air systems, aims to leverage complementary strengths for quicker market access and innovation.

stories.title: Only 30 people live in this Spanish village which offers cheap land and a peaceful life in the hills to attract new residents
PM Modi-Meloni chemistry: How Italy became the heart of India's Europe bet
stories.summary: India is pivoting towards Europe as traditional partnerships become unreliable. The burgeoning India-Italy relationship, spearheaded by Prime Ministers Modi and Meloni, is central to this strategy. This partnership is building crucial economic architecture, including the India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor and a potential EU Free Trade Agreement, positioning Europe as India's primary strategic focus.

stories.title: California hit-and-run: Indian man arrested by ICE after state releases him, 4-year-old victim expected to survive
'I, Vadasseri Damodara Menon Satheesan': Why Kerala Congress leaders are not happy with their own CM
stories.summary: Kerala CM VD Satheesan faces a political storm over using his full legal name, including 'Menon', during his oath. Critics within his party argue it contradicts the Congress's secular image and signals caste politics. Satheesan defended the move, stating it was to honor his late parents, not a political statement.

stories.title: 'Won’t stop until Dharmendra Pradhan resigns': Rahul Gandhi targets Centre over NEET paper leak, action by cops against protesters
stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi has demanded Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation over the NEET paper leak, accusing the Centre of neglecting student concerns. He pledged the Congress's continued fight for affected students, advocating for a robust examination system.

stories.title: Massive car crash in New Jersey pushes BMW into river; Indian-origin driver arrested after fleeing scene on foot
Scientists found fossil pollen that revealed a hidden Nile channel used to build the Great Pyramid
stories.summary: Ancient Egyptians ingeniously utilized a forgotten, high-volume Nile branch, the Khufu Branch, to transport massive pyramid stones. Scientific evidence reveals this 'water highway' flowed directly to Giza, proving they worked smarter, not harder. This natural waterway, sustained by a wetter climate, facilitated efficient logistics, solving the mystery of pyramid construction.

stories.title: Scientists say this oral spray may finally cure your dog’s nasty breath
stories.summary: Bad dog breath is a common issue for pet owners. Scientists have discovered a new solution in sugarcane molasses. This agricultural waste contains compounds that fight odor-causing bacteria in dogs' mouths. A simple spray made from molasses extract has shown immediate and lasting results. It neutralizes bad smells and reduces harmful bacteria. This natural treatment could revolutionize pet dental care.

stories.title: How do erasers actually work? It’s more complicated than you think
stories.summary: Pencil marks, composed of graphite flakes, adhere to paper fibers through weak van der Waals interactions. Erasers, with a higher affinity for graphite, mechanically lift and trap these flakes while also slightly abrading the paper. Unlike pencil, ink seeps into paper, requiring erasable pens to use heat-activated chemistry to render ink transparent.

stories.title: British radio Caroline apologises for accidental King Charles III death broadcast
Oxford AI expert Michael Wooldridge says robot takeover fears miss Big Tech’s real danger
stories.summary: Life's constant negotiations often feel like a rigged game, but Oxford professor Michael Wooldridge argues we can escape the 'zero-sum mindset.' His book, drawing from game theory, reveals most interactions aren't win-or-lose. By understanding strategic thinking, we can foster cooperation, even in AI and business, leading to more fulfilling outcomes for everyone.

stories.title: Inside the Belgium-sized wilderness home to Earth’s highest waterfall and monkey-hunting eagles
stories.summary: Venezuela's Canaima National Park offers a journey to a land time forgot, with towering tepuis inspiring 'The Lost World' and 'Up'. These isolated table-top mountains harbor unique ecosystems, acting as living laboratories for evolution. Below, vast savannas teem with giants like jaguars and harpy eagles, while Angel Falls, the world's tallest waterfall, provides a breathtaking spectacle.

International Tea Day 2026: The storm brewing inside India’s favourite cup
stories.summary: India's beloved chai faces unprecedented challenges. Climate stress, rising costs, and global conflicts are impacting tea production and exports, making your daily cup more expensive. Despite these pressures, the nation's deep emotional connection to tea, a symbol of hospitality and connection, ensures its enduring cultural significance.

stories.title: ‘Don't drop it,’ said Prince William as Novak Djokovic handed the 2022 Wimbledon trophy to Prince George
stories.summary: Prince George experienced a memorable moment at Wimbledon's centenary celebration, holding the champion's trophy for the first time. His father, Prince William, humorously warned him not to drop it, leading to a viral family scene. Princess Kate then gently took the trophy, concluding a touching display of royal tradition and childhood learning.

stories.title: Older than we ever thought? The tiny fossil clue that could push animal origins back
stories.summary: Microscopic squiggles found in 890-million-year-old Canadian reef rocks may represent the oldest animal body fossils, potentially pushing back the origin of animal life by 350 million years. These structures, resembling the skeletons of modern sponges, challenge the traditional view of the Cambrian explosion as the definitive start of animal evolution, suggesting early animals coexisted with bacteria in low-oxygen environments.

stories.title: 'Congress insults tricolour abroad': Piyush Goyal slams Rahul Gandhi's 'gaddar' jab at PM Modi
stories.summary: Union Minister Piyush Goyal strongly criticized Rahul Gandhi and the Congress party for using derogatory language against Prime Minister Narendra Modi. Goyal emphasized India's enhanced global reputation and robust strategic partnerships, citing strong ties with the US and significant investment deals secured during Prime Minister Modi's recent foreign visits. These engagements underscore India's growing influence and trusted partnership status worldwide.

stories.title: In 2021, a 4-year-old girl walking on a beach spotted a mark in a rock that turned out to be a dinosaur footprint
stories.summary: A remarkable dinosaur footprint, 220 million years old, was found by a young girl in Wales. This trace fossil offers insights into prehistoric life and animal behavior. Scientists are studying the ancient track to understand dinosaur movement. The discovery emphasizes that important finds can be made through simple observation, reminding us of Earth's deep history.

stories.title: The tiny piece of amber that proves Antarctica was once a green rainforest
stories.summary: Scientists have discovered a fossilised piece of amber deep beneath the West Antarctic Ice Sheet, providing the first evidence of amber on the continent. This ancient tree resin indicates that Antarctica was once a warm, humid rainforest, challenging current perceptions of the frozen continent and highlighting the dramatic impact of global temperature fluctuations on Earth's ecosystems.

stories.title: Why John D. Rockefeller called the University of Chicago his best investment
stories.summary: Industrialist John D. Rockefeller revolutionised philanthropy by making his University of Chicago donation conditional, demanding local financial buy-in. This strategic approach fostered accountability and community engagement, transforming a seed donation into a self-sustaining powerhouse. This model ensured long-term institutional strength and independent governance, proving that investing in human potential creates legacies larger than any individual.

stories.title: When Jeff Bezos gave the Smithsonian $200 million, the impact went far beyond one museum
stories.summary: Tech entrepreneur Jeff Bezos's $200 million donation to the Smithsonian Institution is revolutionising public education. A significant portion is renovating the National Air and Space Museum, while $130 million establishes a new education centre. This strategic investment aims to create an educational legacy, making complex concepts accessible and fostering community exploration for future generations.

stories.title: When Oprah backed Morehouse scholars, the gift reached far beyond tuition
stories.summary: Oprah Winfrey's $25 million, 30-year endowment to Morehouse College redefines educational philanthropy. Moving beyond mere tuition, this initiative fosters holistic development, including leadership training and global expeditions. This long-term investment cultivates character and creates lasting impact, empowering students for lifelong success and demonstrating the power of sustained support over one-off aid.

stories.title: The night Princess Elizabeth slipped unnoticed into Britain’s VE Day celebrations
stories.summary: On VE Day, 1945, Princess Elizabeth and her sister Margaret famously mingled incognito with jubilant London crowds. This remarkable, humanizing moment saw the future Queen experiencing the nation's relief firsthand, unnoticed amidst the celebrations. The story's enduring appeal lies in this rare glimpse of royalty becoming part of history's fabric, a personal connection to a monumental event.

stories.title: When David Attenborough met Prince George, one giant shark tooth stole the moment
stories.summary: A prehistoric shark tooth gifted by Sir David Attenborough to Prince George at Kensington Palace captivated the world. This massive fossil, from the extinct Otodus megalodon, offered a glimpse into ancient oceans and sparked a brief international dispute over its origin. The image's enduring appeal lies in its blend of royal formality, scientific wonder, and a child's natural curiosity.

stories.title: How Meghan Markle’s cookbook grew from one community kitchen into something much bigger
stories.summary: Meghan Markle's cookbook, 'Together: Our Community Cookbook,' emerged from a community kitchen supporting women affected by the Grenfell Tower tragedy. This initiative focused on communal activity and recovery, with food serving as a medium for preserving memory and culture. Markle acted as a connector, amplifying an existing bottom-up project rather than originating it.

stories.title: 'Time will answer': DK Shivakumar on Karnataka CM buzz amid leadership change speculation
stories.summary: Karnataka Deputy Chief Minister DK Shivakumar stated that "time will decide" his potential elevation to Chief Minister, amidst growing speculation of a leadership change in the state's Congress government. This comes as the Siddaramaiah-led government approaches a significant milestone, fueling discussions about a possible power-sharing arrangement.

stories.title: 'Line between defamation & criticism is thin': Delhi HC on Raghav Chadha's personality rights plea

The oath-taking ceremony for the new Congress-led UDF government is scheduled for May 18, with cabinet formation discussions underway.

stories.title: 'Sack Dharmendra Pradhan now': Rahul Gandhi says NEET paper leak 'betrayed' 22 lakh aspirants
stories.summary: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi has intensified his attack on the Centre regarding the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak. He is demanding the immediate removal of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan. The National Testing Agency cancelled the examination due to evidence of question paper circulation. The Central Bureau of Investigation is investigating the matter. The exam will be re-conducted on June 21.

stories.title: 'Pushpa now my responsibility': West Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari warns TMC strongman Jahangir Khan ahead of Falta repolling
Why Robert F. Smith’s Morehouse surprise donation mattered even more after graduation day
stories.summary: Robert F. Smith's 2019 Morehouse College commencement gift stunned graduates by erasing all their student debt, a move that also covered parents' financial burdens. This $34 million donation highlighted the immense pressure of student loans, particularly within African-American communities, and underscored the broader issues of college affordability and wealth disparity.

stories.title: The surprising reason Joan Kroc’s record-breaking Salvation Army gift still changes lives today
stories.summary: Joan Kroc's monumental donation, recognized by Guinness World Records, funded the construction of numerous community centers across the US. These Kroc Centers offer vital recreational, educational, and social services, becoming hubs for community life and fostering social interaction. The legacy ensures sustainable operation, making her gift a tangible and lasting impact on countless lives.

stories.title: Delhi moves from 'Achiever' to 'Exemplar' category in LEADS 2025
stories.summary: Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta on Saturday said that the national capital has secured a place in the highest 'Exemplar' category in the Logistics Ease Across Different States (LEADS) 2025 Index, marking a major jump from its earlier 'Achiever' status.

stories.title: 'He couldn’t stop blushing': When Queen Elizabeth II smiled at Prince Harry, his reaction said everything
stories.summary: A heartwarming photograph of Queen Elizabeth II beaming with pride at Prince Harry's 2006 military graduation is captivating social media. The image highlights their tender bond, with experts noting the Queen's affection and Harry's youthful demeanor. This touching moment, showcasing a proud grandmother, resonates deeply with royal fans amidst more formal portrayals.

stories.title: Tamil Nadu cabinet: 10 ministers allotted portfolios, CM Vijay keeps home, police & public administration
stories.summary: The Tamil Nadu Lok Bhavan has announced portfolio allocations for the new cabinet. Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay will lead the government. He has retained key departments. Other ministers have been assigned portfolios including finance, health, and education. This marks a significant administrative development for the new government.

stories.title: Did foreigners vote in Tamil Nadu polls? ECI orders probe after 10 detained at Chennai and Madurai airports
Far-right agitators barred from entering UK ahead of anti-Islam activist Tommy Robinson rally
'Misquoted my oral observations': CJI Surya Kant clarifies 'cockroach' remarks on unemployed youth
stories.summary: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant clarified his remarks comparing some unemployed youth to 'cockroaches,' stating his comments were misquoted and targeted individuals using fake degrees in professions. He expressed pride in India's youth, calling them pillars of a developed nation, and emphasized his respect for them. The clarification followed controversy over his observations during a court hearing.

stories.title: ‘We are devastated’: Father shares pain of losing ‘kind-hearted’ son to meningitis in England
What's 'jihadi drug'? Rs 182 crore Captagon seized under Operation Ragepill
stories.summary: India has achieved a significant breakthrough in its fight against drug trafficking with the first-ever seizure of Captagon, dubbed the 'Jihadi drug', worth Rs 182 crore. Under 'Operation Ragepill', authorities intercepted 227.7 kg of the substance, destined for the Middle East, and arrested a foreign national. This operation underscores the government's zero-tolerance policy against narcotics.

Ebola outbreak in DR Congo: Over 80 dead, 246 cases reported in Ituri province; health emergency declared
‘Decade of crises for world’: PM Modi warns ‘past achievements could be wiped away’ by Middle East war
stories.summary: Prime Minister Modi warned that ongoing global conflicts and instability risk undoing decades of development and plunging populations into poverty. Addressing the Indian diaspora in The Hague, he emphasized the critical need for resilient and trusted global supply chains, highlighting India's cooperation with the Netherlands in this area. He also celebrated the diaspora's cultural preservation and India's recent economic transformation.

Meningitis outbreak sparks alarm after student dies and 2 others fall ill in Reading Area
stories.summary: Health authorities are investigating a meningitis outbreak in the Reading and Oxfordshire area after one student died and two others were hospitalized. The cases appear linked through social groups of young people, prompting concern and precautionary measures. Experts urge vigilance for symptoms, especially in teenagers and young adults.

stories.title: 'People are forced to travel in bullock carts': Congress stages protest over fuel, milk price hike
stories.summary: Congress workers protested rising fuel and milk prices, with leaders arriving by bullock cart to highlight inflation's impact. Delhi Congress president Devendra Yadav criticized the government's handling of essential commodity costs, stating inflation has doubled since 2014. This demonstration follows a recent Rs 3 per litre hike in petrol and diesel prices across major cities.

stories.title: BBC’s 72-year Commonwealth Games era ends as Channel 5 secures Glasgow 2026 highlights deal
stories.summary: For the first time in 72 years, the BBC will not broadcast the Commonwealth Games. Channel 5 will air daily highlights of the Glasgow 2026 event, following TNT Sports securing live rights. This shift reflects the BBC's financial pressures and a strategic pivot towards digital content, while Channel 5 expands its sports offerings.

stories.title: NEET-UG paper leak row: Doctors' body calls for dissolution of NTA, files plea in Supreme Court
stories.summary: Doctors' body UDF has petitioned the Supreme Court to dissolve the National Testing Agency, citing a "catastrophic failure" in the NEET-UG 2026 exam's conduct due to alleged paper leaks. The plea also demands significant reforms for transparency and fairness in national entrance tests, aiming to prevent future irregularities.

stories.title: After Donald Trump, Putin to visit China's Xi Jinping on May 19 for two days
stories.summary: Russian President Putin is set for a significant two-day visit to China, commencing May 19, to deepen strategic ties with President Xi Jinping. This follows closely on the heels of Donald Trump's high-profile trip to Beijing, which focused on Taiwan, trade, and Iran. The leaders will discuss strengthening their partnership and address key global issues, aiming to sign a joint declaration.

stories.title: 'If it continues to harbour terrorists ...': Army chief Upendra Dwivedi's stern warning to Pakistan
stories.summary: Army chief Upendra Dwivedi issued a stark warning to Pakistan, stating that continued harboring of terrorists and operations against India would force them to "decide whether they want to be part of geography or history." This statement comes after the first anniversary of Operation Sindoor, where Indian forces conducted precision strikes on terror infrastructure.

stories.title: 'ED is being managed by govt': Robert Vadra gets bail in Gurugram land deal scam case
'Who paid for your globetrotting?': BJP claims Rahul Gandhi took 54 foreign trips in 22 years, costing Rs 60 crore
stories.summary: The BJP has accused Rahul Gandhi of a significant financial discrepancy, alleging his foreign travels over two decades cost approximately Rs 60 crore, far exceeding his declared income. The party questions potential Foreign Contribution Regulation Act and tax law violations, demanding transparency regarding the source of funds for his numerous international trips.

stories.title: ‘Will erode goodwill’: Congress warns Vijay against inducting rebel AIADMK MLAs into Tamil Nadu govt
stories.summary: Congress has cautioned Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay against incorporating rebel AIADMK members into his government. Karti Chidambaram stressed that the public mandate was for a government independent of both AIADMK and DMK. Inducting the splinter group, he warned, would significantly damage Vijay's goodwill and credibility, urging him to remain true to the electoral mandate.

stories.title: Op Epic Fury to resume? Trump weighs fresh Iran strikes after China visit: Report
stories.summary: As US President Trump returns from China, pressure mounts over Iran. Top aides are reportedly preparing options for renewed military action against Tehran if diplomacy falters, including intensified bombing and potential Special Operations deployments. Iran, meanwhile, signals readiness for conflict, while the Strait of Hormuz remains a critical concern for global oil prices.

stories.title: Covid-19 death toll nearly three times higher than official count: WHO
stories.summary: 22.1 million excess deaths recorded globally between 2020 and 2023

stories.title: From semiconductors to water - what’s on PM Modi’s Netherlands agenda
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi arrived in the Netherlands for the second leg of his five-nation tour, aiming to deepen bilateral ties. He will hold talks with Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten, call on King Willem-Alexander and Queen Maxima, and address the Indian community.

stories.title: After Trump’s Beijing visit, Taiwan detects Chinese naval vessels near its waters
stories.summary: Taiwan's defense ministry reported eight Chinese naval vessels near the island following US President Trump's China visit. Trump suggested China might act against Taiwan after his term, acknowledging Beijing's strong objections to its independence. The US arms package for Taiwan remains under review amid escalating tensions and China's territorial claims.

stories.title: Stay clear of Aravalis till we decide its definition, says SC
Lil Tjay sparks backlash after exposing private messages linked to Kai Cenat’s ex-girlfriend
stories.summary: Lil Tjay sparked online backlash after briefly posting and deleting screenshots of private messages allegedly involving Kai Cenat’s ex-girlfriend, Gigi Alayah. Fans criticised the rapper for exposing personal conversations, while others defended his actions amid ongoing tension with Cenat. The streamer has not publicly responded, and the controversy has already reignited debates about clout-chasing, celebrity privacy, and social media drama in entertainment culture.

stories.title: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz: I wouldn’t advise my kids to live or study in US
stories.summary: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz advised his children against studying or working in the US due to a rapidly changing social climate and job market difficulties for the highly educated. Merz expressed strong optimism about Germany's opportunities for young people, contrasting it with his concerns about the current US situation.

"Erika wanted his position": Candace Owens reacts after Charlie Kirk reportedly named wife Erika as TPUSA successor before assassination
stories.summary: Candace Owens has questioned claims that Charlie Kirk chose wife Erika Kirk as his successor at Turning Point USA before his assassination. Owens cast doubt on the authenticity of an audio recording allegedly captured during a private Aspen donor retreat and demanded the release of full video footage. TPUSA has refused, citing donor privacy concerns, further fueling online debate and controversy.

What happened between Benny Johnson and Marjorie Taylor Greene? YouTuber faces grifting accusations during Thomas Massie controversy
stories.summary: Benny Johnson and Marjorie Taylor Greene became involved in a major online feud after Greene criticized Johnson’s YouTube coverage of hush-money allegations against Thomas Massie. The fight quickly turned personal, with both accusing each other of dishonesty and propaganda. Meanwhile, Massie strongly denied the accusations, calling them false and politically motivated just before his Kentucky primary election.

Chud the Builder visibly disappointed as bond hits $1.25 million
stories.summary: Popular streamer Chud the Builder, real name Dalton Eatherly, appeared visibly upset in court after a judge set his bond at $1.25 million. He faces serious charges including attempted murder following a shooting outside a Tennessee courthouse. Eatherly claims he acted in self-defense, but authorities are investigating the incident as a violent crime.

Trump-Xi summit ends with twist: US staff dump Chinese-issued phones, badges before boarding Air Force One
stories.summary: US staff and press accompanying President Trump reportedly discarded materials from Chinese officials before departing Beijing. This occurred despite public displays of goodwill, as behind-the-scenes tensions over security and media access surfaced during the visit, echoing past diplomatic friction.

stories.title: Meningitis outbreak in Berkshire causes panic in three schools
stories.summary: A student's death from meningitis at Henley College has prompted health officials to investigate links to Reading Blue Coat and Highdown Secondary schools. While the Berkshire strain differs from the Kent outbreak, authorities are providing precautionary treatment to close contacts. Experts emphasize the disease requires close contact to spread, with wider public risk remaining low.
